# Changelog

This file records user-visible changes before they are committed. New work should
be added here first, then marked `Committed` or `Pushed` after the git action.

- 2026-08-06 19:56 EDT (-0400) - Sync copy-trading retrospectives to Shared Brain
  - Status: Uncommitted, active in the local copy-trading daemon, and not included in a desktop release.
  - User-facing release note: Agent-analyzed copy trading now keeps its fast local paper-learning state and also synchronizes each matured trade retrospective into Shared Brain. The first 24-hour or target-exit result creates one canonical learning; a later result evolves that same memory with the new evidence instead of creating a duplicate.
  - Safety and failure boundary: Local copy-trading state is persisted before any Brain write and remains the execution source of truth. Shared Brain sync runs outside the signal-polling path, retries with bounded backoff, and cannot block, roll back, promote, or authorize live trading. Acting and copied wallet addresses are excluded from the memory payload and canonical key; model-derived summaries are explicitly stored as evidence, not instructions.

Whole-project TypeScript, focused zero-warning ESLint, the standalone daemon bundle, public roadmap contract, website TypeScript, the optimized 56-route website build, localhost roadmap HTTP/content checks, and scoped whitespace checks pass. The launchd daemon was restarted only after confirming both enabled configs were paper-only; all 36 matured active paper trades now have synced receipts, zero pending/failed receipts, and all 36 receipt IDs resolve to active Shared Brain heads. The reviewed copy-trading v3 Shared Brain decision was evolved from the former local-only contract to the new local-first sync contract. The broad desktop production build remains unverified: its first attempt exhausted Node's roughly 4.1 GB heap and the bounded retry reached the repository's 5 GB process-tree cap at 5.096 GB; no copy-trading diagnostic was emitted before either resource stop.
  - Recovery: Revert only the copy-trading Brain sync service, its state/UI wiring and tests, the roadmap wording, and this entry. Existing local paper records and any already-synchronized Shared Brain memories remain durable evidence and are not deleted automatically.
  - Intended commit message: `feat(copy-trading): sync retrospectives to Shared Brain`

- 2026-08-06 19:17 EDT (-0400) - Make large Work Boards responsive
  - Status: Uncommitted and not included in a desktop release.
  - User-facing release note: Work Boards with hundreds of completed or Needs You tasks now open and respond without rendering the entire backlog at once. Each lane starts with 20 cards and exposes clear incremental loading, while selected/deep-linked cards remain available. Background badges and unchanged refreshes no longer transfer the full board.
  - Root cause and measured baseline: The live default board contained 994 visible cards and produced a 22.41 MiB read because every task was serialized in both `board.tasks` and `columns`. The page mounted 58,044 DOM nodes; opening quick-add took 10.903 seconds and closing it took 7.391 seconds, with individual browser main-thread stalls as long as 2.896 seconds. The native app main thread was idle during sampling, ruling out the previously fixed synchronous dashboard-state write as the primary current cause.
  - Areas changed: lean and revision-aware Kanban HTTP/native reads, count-only background badge reads, compact PATCH responses, local task reconciliation, bounded Work Board lane rendering, duplicate first-load refresh suppression, native bootstrap payload size, focused workflow contracts, and this changelog (`src/app/api/kanban/route.ts`, `src/lib/native/kanban.ts`, `src-tauri/src/{kanban.rs,lib.rs}`, dashboard Work Board hooks/view/styles/types, `scripts/test-kanban-workflow.mjs`, and `CHANGELOG.md`).
  - Verification: Whole-project TypeScript, focused ESLint with no errors, native `cargo check`, the Kanban workflow suite, the dashboard-navigation contract, and scoped whitespace checks pass. The authenticated live route now renders 45 cards in 3,280 DOM nodes, exposes two incremental-load controls, disables add actions during initial hydration, and reports no page errors. After load, opening quick-add fell from 10.903 seconds to 0.257 seconds and closing it fell from 7.391 seconds to 0.179 seconds. The initial board response fell from 23,499,502 to 11,960,140 bytes; unchanged polls are 56 bytes and off-board badge reads are 124 bytes. Whole-crate `cargo fmt --check` remains red on broad pre-existing formatting drift, while the native crate compiles successfully.
  - Recovery: Revert only this entry and the scoped Work Board/API/native changes. No board, task, comment, run, vault, or dashboard-state data was migrated or deleted; the legacy full response remains the default unless a caller requests the lean form.
  - Intended commit message: `fix(work-board): eliminate large-board render and polling stalls`

  - Status: Pushed.

  - Status: Pushed.

- 2026-07-17 22:40:00 EDT (-0400) - Chat App Builder previews survive collector restarts, and a stopped preview says so instead of "The hosted app did not respond."
  - Status: Pushed to `main` in `c7424014`.
  - User-facing release note: Chat-thread App Builder preview servers are children of the fleet collector, so every collector restart/self-reload silently killed them — confirmed twice on a fleet Linux box, where projects flipped to lastError "The app preview process exited and can be restarted." within seconds of collector boot, and the chat Preview pane then showed only the generic "The hosted app did not respond." (the `/api/chat/preview` SSRF gate 403'd the stale URL and PreviewFrame never reads the error envelope). Two fixes. (1) Resilience: at boot the collector now sweeps the registered local app-builder projects and restarts any whose manifest says the runtime was interrupted — a stale "running" manifest with a dead pid, or a status-reconcile-stamped exited stop. It restarts on the project's previous port when free (so stale preview URLs keep working), falls back to a fresh port on EADDRINUSE, goes through the shared adapter's CONFIRM_APP_RUNTIME start contract (it only restores an already-confirmed running state), and never touches a user-requested stop (stop clears lastError; the sweep distinguishes on that). Foreign registry entries (other machines' checkouts, managed backends) are skipped quietly. (2) Honest preview state: when the preview gate rejects a URL that belongs to the thread's own registered project, the route now returns the project's real state instead of a generic 403 — stopped ("The app preview stopped — press Preview to restart it."), errored (the manifest's real lastError + "Press Preview to retry."), or restarted-elsewhere ("The app preview restarted on a new address. Press Preview to reconnect." when an auto-restart landed on a new port). The URL is still never probed on that path, and unknown URLs keep the generic 403 refusal. PreviewFrame titles the empty state by that status ("<app> is not running" / "could not start" / "restarted"). Prerequisite note: this session found the working tree missing origin/main commit b81216925's app-builder cluster (the status reconcile that stamps the exited lastError, the collector-recovery module + suite, the collector's appBuilderContractVersion capability advertisement) — those six files were restored to origin/main content first and both fixes built on top, so this change is also what re-converges the local tree with the already-deployed fleet behavior for these paths.
  - Areas changed: `scripts/lib/app-builder.mjs` (restored from origin/main; + exported `APP_BUILDER_RUNTIME_EXITED_MESSAGE`, new `restartInterruptedLocalAppProject`); new `scripts/lib/app-builder-boot-reconcile.mjs` (boot sweep, extracted to keep the ratcheted collector delta at +2 lines); `scripts/agent-telemetry-collector.mjs` (boot-reconcile import + call in the listen callback; restored origin's `appBuilder`/`appBuilderContractVersion` capability line); `src/lib/services/chat/chat-preview-guard.ts` (`describeThreadAppPreviewOutage`); `src/app/api/chat/preview/route.ts` (outage branch before the 403); `src/features/dashboard/views/chat/exchange/ContextShelf.tsx` (PreviewFrame reads `projectStatus`, status-aware empty-state titles); restored from origin/main verbatim: `src/app/api/app-builder/route.ts`, `src/lib/services/app-builder/collector-recovery.ts`, `scripts/test-app-builder-collector-recovery.mjs`, `scripts/test-app-builder-contract.mjs` (+ new boot-reconcile pins), `scripts/test-app-builder-local.mjs` (+ three new restart/sweep tests); `package.json` (`test:app-builder` runs the restored collector-recovery suite, matching origin).
  - Verification: `pnpm test:app-builder` green (16/16 node:test cases incl. the three new ones: interrupted-runtime restart preserves port/previewUrl and leaves a live runtime alone; reconcile-stamped exited stop restarts while a user-requested stop never does; the boot sweep restarts exactly the interrupted local project from a mixed registry with zero warnings for foreign entries — all with real spawned static servers and SIGKILL). `pnpm test:chat-preview-targets` green (8 new `describeThreadAppPreviewOutage` assertions: stopped/clean-stop/error/moved payloads, and null for identity-mismatch/unknown/off-fleet so the 403 refusal is preserved). `pnpm typecheck` clean; targeted eslint clean on all edited TS/TSX; `node --check` clean on the collector + new module. **Runtime-verified at the real route** against a throwaway-auth verify dev server (5051, new launch.json entry): created + started a real static project via authed `/api/app-builder`, probed `/api/chat/preview` live (`live:true`), SIGKILL'd the preview process and re-probed — got exactly `{live:false, dead:true, projectStatus:"stopped", reason:"The app preview stopped — press Preview to restart it."}` (proving route → status-reconcile → outage chain end-to-end); restarted via the API onto a new port and probed the OLD url — got the "restarted on a new address" payload; probed an off-fleet URL with a valid identity — got the generic 403 refusal with real targets (this last case initially returned the stopped story for ANY url, which is why the helper now requires the probed URL to pass `isFleetCollectorUrl` first). - 2026-07-17 23:24:55 EDT (-0400) - Fleet Update no longer restart-loops machines whose only "dirt" is agent work in the checkout
  - Status: Pushed.
  - User-facing release note: Confirmed on a fleet Linux box (2026-07-18, six collector restarts in 30 minutes): chat App Builder projects are created under the chat working directory's `scratchpad/` folder, which on remote agents is often the collector checkout itself. Those untracked files made the collector's `/health` report `version.dirty=true` forever, and the fleet update route treated dirty alone as update-needed — so every Update press ran the full reinstall through the linkd shell, restarting the collector (which kills its app-preview child processes) without ever cleaning the files, looping forever. Three fixes together: (1) `scratchpad/` is now gitignored at the repo root (unanchored, so nested working directories inside a checkout are covered; deployed collectors inherit it on their next pull). (2) The update route no longer treats local changes alone as update-needed: a machine that is commit-current with all required capabilities now returns an explicit "up to date with local changes present … agent work in the checkout is left alone" result instead of reinstalling, and the fleet panel shows that message. A dirty checkout that is also behind still updates via the commit comparison. (3) The collector's dirty computation itself (`/health` version) now excludes untracked `scratchpad/` entries, so already-deployed dirt stops reporting dirty as soon as the machine picks up new collector code — modified tracked files still count as real divergence. Related but separate (already tracked, not duplicated here): auto-restarting preview servers after collector restarts.
  - Areas changed: `.gitignore` (root `scratchpad/` rule); `src/app/api/fleet/update/route.ts` (`updateNeededBefore` drops the dirty trigger; `already-current` response carries `localChanges` + explicit message); `src/features/dashboard/hooks/use-fleet-notifications-controller.tsx` (already-current detail prefers the route's message); `scripts/lib/collector-source-version.mjs` (new exported `collectorCheckoutDirty` filters untracked scratchpad entries; wired into `readCollectorAppVersion`); tests in `scripts/test-collector-windows-update.mjs` (9 unit cases + an end-to-end `readCollectorAppVersion` dirty=false case) and `scripts/test-chat-maintenance-safety.mjs` (pins: `updateNeededBefore` contains no dirty trigger, the explicit up-to-date-with-local-changes result exists, the collector dirty flag routes through `collectorCheckoutDirty`, and the root `.gitignore` has the `scratchpad/` rule).
  - Verification: full gate baseline before the change 223/224 (sole red: the standing `check-sizes` ratchet on 7 concurrent-dirty legacy files) → after 223/224 with the identical `check-sizes` set and line counts — no regressions, and none of the 7 files were touched. `pnpm test:collector-windows-update` and `pnpm test:chat-maintenance-safety` green standalone. `pnpm typecheck` clean; `eslint` exit 0 on both edited TS files; `node --check` clean on the edited mjs files. `git check-ignore -v` confirms the new rule matches both `scratchpad/...` and `agents/workdir/scratchpad/...`; the pre-existing tracked `scratchpad/barge-in-wiring-sim.mjs` stays tracked (gitignore does not affect tracked files) and its modifications would still count as dirty — named as a pre-existing committed agent dropping, left alone. Auto-update was checked and is NOT part of the loop (it only fires on state "stale", which ignores dirty). NOT runtime-verified: the healed loop on the real affected box — that needs one more Update cycle after this lands so the box pulls the new `.gitignore`/collector code; with fix (2) the reinstall already stops firing on dirty-only regardless.
  - Rollback: revert the `.gitignore` hunk, the two route hunks, the one-line controller hunk, and the `collector-source-version.mjs` hunk (restore `dirty: dirty.length > 0` and the `dirty` destructure name); drop the two test additions.
  - Intended commit message: `fix(fleet): stop dirty-only update restart loops — gitignore chat scratchpad projects, make dirty-but-current a no-op, exclude agent droppings from collector dirty`

- 2026-07-17 22:40:00 EDT (-0400) - Chat App Builder previews survive collector restarts, and a stopped preview says so instead of "The hosted app did not respond."
  - Status: Pushed.

(the `/api/chat/preview` SSRF gate 403'd the stale URL and PreviewFrame never reads the error envelope). Two fixes. (1) Resilience: at boot the collector now sweeps the registered local app-builder projects and restarts any whose manifest says the runtime was interrupted — a stale "running" manifest with a dead pid, or a status-reconcile-stamped exited stop. It restarts on the project's previous port when free (so stale preview URLs keep working), falls back to a fresh port on EADDRINUSE, goes through the shared adapter's CONFIRM_APP_RUNTIME start contract (it only restores an already-confirmed running state), and never touches a user-requested stop (stop clears lastError; the sweep distinguishes on that). Foreign registry entries (other machines' checkouts, managed backends) are skipped quietly. (2) Honest preview state: when the preview gate rejects a URL that belongs to the thread's own registered project, the route now returns the project's real state instead of a generic 403 — stopped ("The app preview stopped — press Preview to restart it."), errored (the manifest's real lastError + "Press Preview to retry."), or restarted-elsewhere ("The app preview restarted on a new address. Press Preview to reconnect." when an auto-restart landed on a new port). The URL is still never probed on that path, and unknown URLs keep the generic 403 refusal. PreviewFrame titles the empty state by that status ("<app> is not running" / "could not start" / "restarted"). Prerequisite note: this session found the working tree missing origin/main commit b81216925's app-builder cluster (the status reconcile that stamps the exited lastError, the collector-recovery module + suite, the collector's appBuilderContractVersion capability advertisement) — those six files were restored to origin/main content first and both fixes built on top, so this change is also what re-converges the local tree with the already-deployed fleet behavior for these paths.

- 2026-07-17 18:33:00 EDT (-0400) - Fleet Shell panel stops pretending Windows machines have a remote shell, and shell errors read as errors instead of JSON parse crashes
  - Status: Pushed to `main` in `c7424014`.
  - User-facing release note: Observed live against a Windows fleet PC: the machine Shell panel was offered for Windows machines even though Windows hivemind-linkd builds run without the remote shell service (`cmd/hivemind-linkd/main.go` gates it on GOOS; the unix-shell spawn in `shell.go`/`shell_unix.go` has no Windows counterpart), and when the request failed, linkd's Go reverse proxy answered with a plain-text body ("hivemind-linkd proxy error: dial tcp 127.0.0.1:8787: connectex: ...") that the dashboard's shell route re-parsed as JSON — surfacing a raw `Unexpected token 'h', "hivemind-l"... is not valid JSON` crash at the bottom of the terminal modal. Now: (1) the Shell affordance is gated per machine through a new single-sourced predicate — a machine-reported capability wins when present (collector `/health` `capabilities.remoteShell`, so a future Windows linkd that gains shell support opens the gate by flipping its own flag with no dashboard change), falling back to the OS predicate (`isWindowsMachineOs`, both "windows" and "win32" spellings) for collectors that predate the flag. The hive-view Shell chip renders disabled with an explanatory title, the classic-view Terminal button dims with an explanatory tooltip (aria-disabled, not disabled, so the tooltip still fires), and the terminal modal itself — the choke point every entry path goes through — shows a clear "Remote shell isn't available on <machine> yet" state instead of wiring up a dead SSE stream. (2) The shell route now reads upstream bodies as text and forwards JSON verbatim, wrapping any non-JSON body as `{ ok: false, error: <the text> }` (non-JSON 2xx maps to 502), so the panel renders linkd's plain-text failures as a readable error line. (3) linkd itself answers `/_hivemind/shell/*` with a JSON 501 envelope on shell-less hosts (Windows builds, `-shell=false`) on both the tailnet listener and the loopback control API, instead of falling through to the collector proxy — the exact fall-through that produced the observed dial-error body.
  - Areas changed: `src/features/fleet/fleet-identity.ts` (`isWindowsMachineOs`, `machineRemoteShellAvailable`); `scripts/agent-telemetry-collector.mjs` (`capabilities.remoteShell`, one line); `src/app/api/fleet/discover/route.ts` + `src/lib/types/agent-runtime.ts` (`remoteShell?: boolean` on the collector-capabilities types); `src/components/fleet/fleet-data.ts` (`FleetMachine.remoteShell`); `src/features/dashboard/hooks/use-dashboard-derived-state.tsx` (mapper computes it from capability → OS → `system.platform` fallback); `src/components/fleet/machine-terminal-modal.tsx` (unavailable state, no SSE/fetch wiring); `src/components/fleet-hive/HivePanel.tsx` (disabled Shell chip); `src/components/fleet/selection-tooltip.tsx` (dimmed Terminal button + tooltip); `src/app/api/fleet/shell/shell-target.ts` (`shellEnvelopeFromUpstream`) + `src/app/api/fleet/shell/route.ts` (GET/POST use it; the stream route already handled text bodies); `cmd/hivemind-linkd/shell.go` (`serveShellUnavailable`) + `main.go` (tailnet handler + control mux answer shell paths with it when the service is off) + `shell_test.go` (JSON-501 test); new `scripts/test-fleet-shell-availability.mjs` registered as `test:fleet-shell-availability` in `package.json` + `scripts/test-gate.mjs`.
  - Verification: new hermetic suite green standalone and in the gate (predicate matrix incl. capability-overrides-OS both directions, envelope wrap of the exact observed proxy-error body, non-JSON-2xx→502, UI wiring pins); `go build` green for host and `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64`; `go test ./cmd/hivemind-linkd/` green including the new 501 test; `pnpm typecheck` clean standalone; targeted `eslint` 0 errors on all edited TS/TSX files. NOT runtime-verified: the terminal modal's unavailable state (unreachable from the gated chips by design; wiring pinned by the hermetic suite) and the linkd JSON-501 on a real Windows box (deployed Windows linkd binaries keep the plain-text fall-through until their next update — the route wrap covers them meanwhile). - 2026-07-17 18:20:00 EDT (-0400) - Windows setup re-runs actually apply updates: installer restarts the stale collector, and the first-run wizard can no longer fake instant completion
  - Status: Pushed to `main` in `c7424014`.
  - User-facing release note: Re-running setup on a Windows machine now genuinely updates it. Two defects confirmed live on a Windows fleet PC (reported cross-session while delivering the env-sync fix): (1) `scripts/install-telemetry-collector.ps1` never stopped a previously-running collector — it re-registered the task with `-Force` (which does not touch a running instance), "started" it (a no-op on a running task), and then verified `/health` against the STALE process, so multiple full setup re-runs and even an app reinstall left the old collector serving pre-fix code. The installer now stops the collector task and its own node process (command-line matched, never a foreign port owner) BEFORE the port scan — before, so a still-listening stale collector cannot drift the recorded port — waits for the port to free, and proceeds; this is the Windows analog of the Unix installer restarting its service on every run. (2) The first-run wizard's done-gate was "a collector answers on 8787", so with a stale collector listening, re-run setup flipped to the completed screen in under a second regardless of whether the hidden setup script ran, failed, or was still mid-download. - 2026-07-17 17:05:00 EDT (-0400) - Windows fleet machines can now be updated remotely: PowerShell update path + working self-reload restart + version identity for git-free checkouts
  - Status: Pushed to `main` in `c7424014`.
  - User-facing release note: Windows machines in the Hive Fleet previously had no update path short of a human re-running setup at the keyboard: the dashboard's Update button silently failed (the collector's update endpoint launched its command through `sh`, which does not exist on Windows, and the update script itself was bash), the remote Hivemind Link shell is intentionally unix-only, and the collector's own reload-on-source-change exited cleanly — which launchd/systemd relaunch but Windows Task Scheduler (restart-on-failure) does not, stranding the collector until the next logon. All three are fixed and validated end-to-end on a real Windows Server 2022 box: the collector now generates and launches a per-platform update command (a new PowerShell updater on Windows, unchanged bash elsewhere) via a handoff to a dedicated "HivemindOS Update" Scheduled Task, the collector's hidden supervisor now relaunches the collector when it exits for a self-reload (restart observed 1.3s after a source change), and git-free archive checkouts (how the desktop app installs `~/.hivemindos/app-source` — stock Windows has no git) now record and report their source commit so the fleet dashboard can tell "up to date" from "update available" and verify an update actually landed (live-verified: /health reported the marker commit, the GitHub-probed latest, and the PowerShell update command). The Windows updater pulls via git when the checkout is a git clone, otherwise overlays the latest GitHub main archive in place (preserving node_modules and local env files), refreshes the collector's single npm dependency, and restarts the collector by re-running the Windows collector installer — stopping only its own collector process (matched by command line, never a port owner) so the recorded port stays stable.
  - Areas changed: `scripts/lib/collector-update-command.mjs` (per-platform launch command + new `collectorManualUpdateCommand` for the /health `updateCommand`; unix strings byte-identical to before); `scripts/lib/collector-update-launcher.mjs` (win32 launches a short-lived NON-detached `powershell.exe` bootstrap instead of `sh -lc`; two real-Windows findings forced this shape — Windows PowerShell's console host exits without executing when spawned with `DETACHED_PROCESS`, and a non-detached child inherits the collector task's Job object, where the update would kill itself when it restarts the collector's task); new `scripts/start-hivemindos-update-task.ps1` (the bootstrap: registers/starts a one-shot "HivemindOS Update" Scheduled Task — own job, S4U with Interactive fallback, hidden-process fallback when Task Scheduler is inaccessible — with the update pipeline passed as `-EncodedCommand` base64 so no quoting is re-parsed en route; the bootstrap's clean exit keeps the maintenance reservation like `systemd-run`, and the restarted collector clears it); `uninstall.ps1` (removes the "HivemindOS Update" task in the collector-task block); new `scripts/update-hivemindos.ps1` (the Windows analog of `update-hivemindos.sh`, collector-focused — the dashboard on Windows is the desktop app, so no dev-server management; handles Windows PowerShell 5.1 returning `Invoke-WebRequest` `.Content` as `byte[]` for the `vnd.github.sha` media type, a live-VM find that also fixed the same latent bug in the setup.rs marker write); new `scripts/lib/collector-source-version.mjs` (`.hivemindos-source-commit` marker read with 40-hex validation, GitHub `application/vnd.github.sha` latest-main probe cached 10 minutes including failures, and `readCollectorAppVersion` extracted from the oversized collector — the collector file shrinks net); `scripts/agent-telemetry-collector.mjs` (delegates `readAppVersion`; self-reload exits **75** on win32 — a real-box test proved Task Scheduler's `-RestartCount`/restart-on-failure NEVER relaunches a task whose process ran and then exited nonzero, so exit codes alone cannot fix the stranding; 9746 → 9741 lines, allowance 9748); `scripts/install-telemetry-collector.ps1` (the generated hidden supervisor `run-collector-hidden.ps1` is now the relauncher, launchd-KeepAlive-style: instant restart on exit 75, 60s-delayed restart on other failures, gives up after three consecutive sub-30s failures so a port-conflict zombie cannot hot-loop, exits clean on 0; artifact already covered by uninstall.ps1); `src-tauri/src/setup.rs` (both archive-bootstrap commands now best-effort record the downloaded source commit into the marker, with the PS 5.1 `byte[]` `.Content` handling; Rust tests extended); new `scripts/test-collector-windows-update.mjs` (hermetic: command/launcher matrix incl. quote-escaping, marker + probe validation and caching, `readCollectorAppVersion` git/marker/unknown cases, wiring pins); - 2026-07-17 16:48:00 EDT (-0400) - Env sync: a renamed machine's system Tailscale node no longer sits in "unreachable" forever
  - Status: Pushed to `main` in `c7424014`.
  - User-facing release note: When a machine's OS hostname changes (macOS auto-renames on mDNS conflicts), its embedded hivemind-linkd tailnet node re-registers under the new name while its system Tailscale node keeps the old sticky MagicDNS name. Env-sync peer accounting folded the two nodes by a hostname heuristic (strip the `hivemindos-` prefix, compare labels), which goes blind after such a rename — so the dead-to-probes system node was reported as a permanently unreachable peer in every sync-maintenance summary, queued env updates for that ghost were retried forever, and reverse-reachability carried a phantom entry. Ready collectors already self-report their system node in `/health` (`tailnetSelf`, the 2026-07-05 fleet-discovery fix); the env-sync dedup now also folds any unreachable node whose MagicDNS name a ready collector claims as its own. Matching uses the unique sticky `dnsName` only — never `tailnetSelf.name`, the OS ComputerName, which distinct machines can share. (Dedup by machineId is impossible for these nodes: the ghost is precisely the node whose collector probe never answers.)
  - Areas changed: `scripts/hive-env-add` (`env_sync_from_collector` now returns the collector's `tailnetSelfDnsName`; `drop_reachable_machine_duplicates` matches it in addition to the hostname-identity heuristic; new `normalized_tailnet_dns` helper); new `scripts/test-env-sync-machine-dedup.mjs` (regression suite: Python unit coverage of the dedup — rename case, pre-rename heuristic, distinct-machine and shared-ComputerName negatives, `-N` suffix preservation — plus a hermetic E2E through the real entry path with a fake `tailscale` CLI on PATH and a stub collector, asserting the maintenance `pull.unreachable` accounting and full no-queue delivery; dead peers use 255.255.255.255 so probes fail synchronously); `package.json` + `scripts/test-gate.mjs` (registered as `test:env-sync-machine-dedup` in the gate).
  - Verification: reproduced the live symptom in the unit harness — the pre-fix HEAD script keeps `liams-macbook-pro-1.tail0000.ts.net` in the unreachable list when only the renamed linkd sibling answers; post-fix it is folded and the E2E maintenance summary lists only the genuinely-dead control peer. New suite green standalone and via pnpm (<1s); neighbor suites `test:env-sync-queue` (standalone), `test:hive-env-add-command`, `test:hive-env-remove`, `test:hive-env-roundtrip` all green. Full gate: 219/220 — sole persistent red is the pre-existing `check-sizes` on five concurrent-dirty legacy files (none touched here; the Python script is outside the ratchet's extension set), plus one run where `test:collector-reserved-profile-snapshots` flaked on temp-dir cleanup (ENOTEMPTY; green standalone and in the other gate runs). The live This-Mac collector still shows the ghost until it runs the fixed script — the 10-minute pull-reconcile loop clears `envSync.maintenance.lastSummary.pull.unreachable` on its own once this lands.
  - Rollback: revert `scripts/hive-env-add`, delete `scripts/test-env-sync-machine-dedup.mjs`, and drop the two registration lines in `package.json`/`scripts/test-gate.mjs`; the extra `tailnetSelfDnsName` key is read only by the dedup, so no other consumer changes shape.

  - Status: Pushed to `main` as `088a0d9b3` (landed via a disposable rebase worktree onto origin/main because the shared checkout's local `main` has 5 unpushed commits — 3b30e5007..4a86ed01a incl. fd4581152 "TONS of improvements" and the df4c34b56 ratchet re-baseline — that origin does not have; local `main` also retains the pre-rebase duplicate commit ad0752792.   - User-facing release note: A freshly set-up Windows fleet machine looked healthy locally but every Mac/Linux peer reported it "unreachable over the Tailnet" in the dashboard's machine panel (observed live on a brand-new Windows desktop 2026-07-17). Root cause: the collector resolved the setup.ps1-installed `hive-env-add.cmd` shim, but only one of its four hive-env-add spawn sites passed `shell: true`, and Node ≥ 20.12.2 (CVE-2024-27980 hardening) refuses to spawn `.cmd` files without it — so `GET /env` (what peers pull env keys from), the 10-minute sync-maintenance loop, and the E2E sync endpoint all failed with `spawn EINVAL`. Peers' env-sync pulls then filed the machine under `unreachable`, and reverse reachability surfaced that as the (misleading) dead-linkd warning while linkd was actually fine. The resolver now prefers invoking the extensionless Python script through a launcher (`py -3` → `python` → `python3`, matching setup.ps1 and `src/lib/services/hive-env-command.ts`) with a real argv — no shell, so arguments stay properly quoted — and keeps the `.cmd`+shell path only as a fallback when no Python launcher resolves; in that fallback, caller-supplied E2E values are charset-guarded so they cannot break out of the cmd.exe line (the shell join would otherwise be an injection vector on a tailnet-reachable endpoint).
  - Areas changed: new `scripts/lib/hive-env-add-command.mjs` (cross-platform resolver, injectable deps, extracted per the oversized-file rule — the collector file shrinks by one line net); `scripts/agent-telemetry-collector.mjs` (resolver delegation; all four spawn sites now spread the resolver argv and pass `shell` + `windowsHide`; E2E shell-fallback value guard; `/health` envSync.command shows the full effective command); new `scripts/test-hive-env-add-command.mjs` (hermetic resolver matrix + static guard that every collector spawn site spreads the argv and passes the shell flag); `package.json` + `scripts/test-gate.mjs` (suite registered in the gate as `test:hive-env-add-command`).
  - Verification: reproduced live before the fix — the Windows PC's collector answered `/health` over the Tailnet in 0.13s but `GET /env` returned 500 `spawn EINVAL`, and its own maintenance status showed `lastError: spawn EINVAL`; This Mac's pull summary listed the PC in both `peers` (health probe OK) and `unreachable` (env fetch failed). New suite green standalone. Baseline full gate before the change: 217/218, sole red `check-sizes` on five concurrent-dirty legacy files (none touched here). Post-change gate: 218/219 — the new suite green, the identical `check-sizes` red with the identical five files, no new failures; the collector file itself shrank one line (9747 → 9746, watermark 9748). Windows-side runtime verification requires the affected PC to pick up the update (no remote update path exists on Windows: linkd's shell is unix-only, the collector's `/update` launches via `sh -lc`, and the self-reload watcher exits 0 which the Task Scheduler restart-on-failure setting does not relaunch) — recorded in this entry once the PC re-runs setup.
  - Rollback: revert the five files in one `git revert`; the resolver fallback preserves the exact pre-change `.cmd`+shell behavior, and no state or contract changes ride along (`/health` envSync.command is display-only — no programmatic consumers, checked repo-wide).
  - Intended commit message: `fix(collector): Windows env sync — spawn hive-env-add via Python launcher argv, not the .cmd shim Node refuses (spawn EINVAL)`

- 2026-07-11 20:34:00 +0800 - Hive Compute becomes a confidential marketplace for any model workload
  - Status: Pushed in `45f3216a5`
  - Areas changed: canonical workload and encrypted-artifact protocol; renter key generation, encrypted local key vault, and encrypted-only large-input spool; capabilities, draft, encrypted input upload, submit, status/cancel, encrypted output download, and acknowledgement API routes; automatic confidential chat transport; generated worker confidential-sidecar routing and full challenge binding; workload/worker/marketplace contracts; context index and Hive Compute user documentation; private compute gateway D1 migrations, per-job Durable Object, private R2 artifact plane, production Azure SEV-SNP plus NVIDIA NRAS verifier, job-scoped attestation, signed metering/settlement, cancellation/refund, retention cleanup, tests, and operator documentation in `../hivemind-cloud-services/workers/compute-gateway`.
  - Summary: Hive Compute now has one typed, asynchronous protocol for image, video, audio, music, speech, 3D, embeddings, reranking, and namespaced custom models instead of a hard-coded image exception. Official asynchronous workload jobs require gateway-verified hardware TEE execution and renter-only output encryption: the outer worker, host operating system and operator, gateway, and artifact store handle ciphertext, metadata, progress, and signed manifests, while clear inputs and generated content exist only inside the attested boundary and on the renter after local decryption. The renter private key is created before draft creation, never leaves the renter, remains encrypted locally until every output artifact is acknowledged and deleted from gateway storage, and is then erased. Large input artifacts are chunk-encrypted locally to a private, atomically finalized `HIVEART1` spool; only encrypted bytes touch disk, and its cleanup handle removes the spool after upload. OpenAI-compatible chat also requires confidential execution and renter-only generated output, although its compatibility request body still terminates at the official gateway before enclave delivery. Plaintext execution compatibility is restricted to an explicitly non-official self-hosted gateway.
  - Model trust UI: The hosted gateway now publishes a model as `Confidential verified` only while a connected worker has fresh, server-verified hardware attestation, verified evidence bytes, a bound completion-signing key, and renter-only encrypted output. HivemindOS shows that trust badge in the model selector and stably orders those direct models before routes that may fall back. Provider self-claims, expired evidence, disconnected workers, key relays, and centralized fallback never receive the badge.

  - Summary: Two safety gaps the completeness critic surfaced. (1) Prompt injection: a prospect's reply preview/subject flowed verbatim (`signal.summary`) into the sales-content draft-reply/pricing/etc. worker prompts and the company dispatch context, so a reply saying "ignore your instructions and…" was read by the agent as instructions. (2) The park-for-approval gate was cooperative: `promote` is exposed to agents through the MCP `work_board` tool with no actor restriction, so a worker (or a prompt-injected one) could move its own parked "Needs You" card back to Ready and resume with no human answer. Promoting a Needs-You card now rejects an agent-originated call (the MCP client tags itself `actor: "agent"`); a human still releases it, and Idea promotion is unaffected.
  - Not done (documented follow-ups): a required independent judge gate on deliverable-producing company tasks (the `makeLoopJudge` machinery exists but the company loop never adds an agent-kind gate); a ground-truth axis on the restaurant contract (compare rendered menu items against the lead's stored business profile); and scheduled/driver-triggered email QA. Each is a larger change and is flagged, not silently skipped. Residual on the promote gate: a raw agent that bypasses the MCP tool and hits `/api/kanban` directly with the device token and no `actor` is not blocked — the fix closes the sanctioned agent path (MCP), which is the documented hole; a route-level actor derivation would close the raw path too.
  - Verification: `pnpm typecheck` passes (exit 0). `pnpm test:untrusted-context` passes. `test-sales-content-machine.mjs` passes with two new assertions that a prospect-derived signal summary is wrapped in `<<<HIVEMINDOS_UNTRUSTED_SOURCE_DATA>>>` in both the dispatch context and the draft-reply prompt. The promote gate was verified END-TO-END through the real route on the live throwaway-auth server (5043): `test-kanban-workflow.mjs` (run with `KANBAN_TEST_BASE_URL=…:5043`) passes, including a new case where an `actor:"agent"` promote of a Needs-You card is rejected ("waiting on a human decision"), the card stays in Needs You, and a human (unflagged) promote then moves it to Ready. Note: agents only pick up the new MCP `work_board` behavior after their MCP server process restarts.

- 2026-07-11 15:01:22 +0800 - Autonomous companies notice prospect replies without a human opening the Cockpit
  - Status: Pushed in `45f3216a5`

  - Summary: A prospect replying to outreach is the moment a company can make money, and it was the moment it went blind: the sales-content engine already reads the inbox, records a `mail.reply_received` event, and plans a draft-reply action whose dispatch context the driver feeds into the next dispatch — but the only thing that triggered that mail read was a human opening the company's Cockpit. NOT verified end-to-end at runtime: a real inbound reply flowing through to a persisted event + notification needs a live mail provider and an actual prospect reply, which this environment can't exercise; the ingestion call, throttle, new-reply diff, and notification are confirmed by compile + integration only. Driver file is 749/1500 lines.
  - Rollback: Remove the `maybeIngestInboundReplies` call from the per-company loop, the helper + its throttle map/const, and the two sales-content imports. No data or schema changes.

(1) The spend ledger had the same wipe/blind-spot bug as the company store: a present-but-unparseable file read as an empty history, so a budget check saw zero spend (an effectively unlimited budget) and the next append persisted only its one record — destroying all spend history. It now fails closed: reads throw `SpendLedgerCorruptError`, so budget checks block the spend and `appendSpend` refuses to overwrite the ledger until it is repaired. Appends are also serialized through an in-process queue and written atomically (tmp + rename) so concurrent spends can't interleave and drop each other's records or leave a torn file. (2) A spend approval is now scoped to the exact action the human approved — same agent, asset, KIND, and TARGET, for at most the approved amount. Previously `matchesGrant` checked only agent + asset + amount, so an approval for "Firecrawl top-up $40 → firecrawl" could be silently consumed by the same agent's next $40 spend of any kind to any destination.

Each needs broader multi-file or cross-repo change and is flagged, not silently skipped.
  - Verification: `pnpm typecheck` passes (exit 0). New `pnpm test:spend-ledger-integrity` passes (exit 0): missing ledger → empty; three concurrent appends all land (none dropped); a corrupt ledger makes `readSpendLedger` reject and `appendSpend` refuse to overwrite it, leaving the bytes intact; and a grant scoped to kind x402 + target firecrawl is not consumed by a kind-`api` or different-target spend, is consumed by the exact action, and can't be reused. Existing money suites still green: `test:wallet-vault`, `test:company-revenue-share`, `test:copy-trading`, `test:veil-auto-send` (exercises `consumeApproval`), `test:wallet-real-tabs`. `test:acting-wallet-context` still fails for its pre-existing baseline reason (explicit-chain robinhood vs base), not regressed. Fixed a strip-only-TS issue proactively: the new error class uses explicit fields, not a constructor parameter property.
  - Rollback: Revert `spend-ledger.ts` (restore `catch → []`, the direct `fs.writeFile`, remove the queue + `SpendLedgerCorruptError`); revert `matchesGrant`/`consumeApproval` to the agent+asset+amount signature and drop the kind/target args at the `spend-governance.ts` call; remove the new test file and its `package.json` + `test-gate.mjs` entries.
  - Intended commit message: `wallet: fail closed on a corrupt spend ledger + scope approval grants to kind and target`

- 2026-07-11 14:40:45 +0800 - Company store fails closed on corruption instead of silently wiping the portfolio
  - Status: Pushed in `45f3216a5`
  - Areas changed: company definitions store (`src/lib/services/companies-store.ts`) — read/write path only; hermetic coverage in `scripts/test-company-vault-store.mjs`.
  - Summary: The companies definitions/local file (Obsidian-editable, Syncthing-replicated) previously read as an empty portfolio whenever it was present but unparseable — a hand-edit typo, a Syncthing conflict, or a disk glitch — and the next config write then persisted (and replicated) that wipe. It now fails closed: a corrupt file throws `CompaniesFileCorruptError` on read and a write refuses to overwrite it, so the portfolio is never silently erased and the bad file is left intact for recovery. Records are normalized on read — a record with no id is dropped with a log instead of crashing the whole read, and a record with an id but no name gets a placeholder so the portfolio sort can't throw (previously one malformed record 500'd the companies API and stalled all dispatch). Every durable write now keeps up to 5 rotated `.bak.N` backups (bounded, so they can't bloat the vault). `writeRaw`'s multi-step persist (overlay write + backup rotation + definitions write) runs under an in-process write queue so concurrent writes can't interleave and corrupt the rotation.
  - Known limits (documented in code, deferred): the queue serializes the write, not the full read-modify-write, so two mutations that each read before either writes can still lose an update within a process; and nothing here serializes writers across processes (5020 + 5021 + Tauri). Rotated backups make those clobbers recoverable; full RMW + cross-process locking is a follow-up.
  - Verification: `pnpm typecheck` passes (exit 0). `pnpm test:company-vault-store` passes (exit 0) with four new assertions: a definitions write leaves a `.bak.0`; a no-id record drops and a nameless record is kept with a placeholder; a corrupt definitions file makes `readCompanies()` reject with `CompaniesFileCorruptError`; and a write refuses to overwrite it, leaving the corrupt bytes intact. Confirmed the two pre-existing red suites in my area (`test:company-autonomy` "15 per-lead URLs survive (got 0)", `test:company-issues` crew-wizard regex) still fail for their original reasons — not regressed by this change. Caught and fixed a strip-only-TS incompatibility: the initial error class used a constructor parameter property, which Node's native type-stripping (used by the hermetic loader) rejects; rewritten with explicit field declarations. File is 1467/1500 lines.
  - Rollback: Revert `companies-store.ts` (restore the `catch → []` read, the direct `writeFileAtomic`, and the `async writeRaw`; remove `CompaniesFileCorruptError`, `normalizeCompanyRecord`, the backup rotation, and the write queue) and drop the added `test-company-vault-store.mjs` assertions.
  - Intended commit message: `companies-store: fail closed on a corrupt portfolio file + normalize records + rotated backups`

  - Status: Pushed in `45f3216a5`
  - Areas changed: conversation excerpt budgeting (`src/lib/services/obsidian/agent-memory/excerpt.ts`: new exported `adaptiveConversationExcerptBudget` with temporal-query detection and global char budgets; segment-safe window cuts that never end inside a bracketed caption); recall hit assembly (`src/lib/services/obsidian/agent-memory/core.ts`: two-pass selection that renders excerpts only for returned hits with the adaptive per-hit budget); semantic recall (`src/lib/services/obsidian/agent-memory/embeddings.ts`: new `fullVaultSemanticScores` lazily embeds conversation-note candidates, bounded at 400, content-hashed; wired into full-vault recall); morphological variant hardening (`src/lib/services/obsidian/agent-memory/query.ts`: 4-char stem floor for -ed/-ing folds); conversation-recall regressions.
  - Summary: Two recall capabilities. First, the per-hit conversation excerpt budget now adapts to the final hit count under a global context budget (84k chars, 168k for aggregation/temporal queries, per-hit cap 4,800), so a ten-session archive is not excerpted through the same keyhole as a ten-thousand-note vault, and excerpt windows never cut inside a bracketed image-caption segment. Whole-project tsc clean outside a concurrently edited companion view. Deterministic probes (soft token-overlap): LoCoMo 95-question hard slice 65/95 → 74/95 and LME multi-session 59/91 → 64/91 with the semantic layer on. Full-suite presence with the adaptive budget alone: LoCoMo 65.8% → 70.3%, LongMemEval 81.0% → 85.8% (context tokens p50 ≈ 12.4k/15.4k). A 120-question seeded sonnet-5 spot-check on adaptive-budget contexts measured conversions statistically unchanged from the prior round (LoCoMo 90/75 present/absent, LME 80/50), keeping projections at ≈85.5/75.7 vs Mem0's 91.8/94.8 before the semantic layer; the semantic-enabled projection is being measured next. - 2026-07-11 12:21:40 +0800 - Recall honors standing user guidance and reaches paraphrased sessions for counting questions
  - Status: Pushed in `45f3216a5`
  - Areas changed: agent-memory conversation excerpts (`src/lib/services/obsidian/agent-memory/excerpt.ts`: standing-guidance channel, aggregation passage coverage, new `isAggregationRecallQuery` export, assistant-grounded exception for the durable-guidance ranking boost); full-vault recall candidate supply and hit assembly (`src/lib/services/obsidian/agent-memory/core.ts`: bounded recent-conversation supplement plus evidence-gated padding for aggregation queries); conversation-recall regressions (`scripts/test-agent-memory-conversation-recall.mjs`).
  - Summary: Two recall behaviors that raw lexical matching cannot provide. First, short durable user instructions ("please always mention the calorie content…") now surface in conversation excerpts even when the topical query shares no vocabulary with them, with a bounded budget slice, dedup against already-selected passages, and an exception for assistant-grounded lookups where a standing instruction must not hijack ranking (that exception also fixes an interaction with the existing durable-guidance ranking boost). Second, counting/summary/journey questions ("how many weddings have I attended?") now reach paraphrased sessions that share no query vocabulary ("Emma's ceremony…"): aggregation-shaped queries pad the hit list toward the caller's limit with the newest conversation sessions (bounded at 150 candidate reads), and the padding only engages when at least one genuinely matched hit exists, so unsupported-question abstention still returns nothing. Aggregation excerpts also cover up to six distinct instances per note instead of four.
  - Verification: TDD red-first for all three behaviors (guidance surfacing, assistant-grounded control, paraphrase-session inclusion with matched-above-padded ordering and unsupported-query abstention); `node scripts/test-agent-memory-conversation-recall.mjs` passes. Recall-sensitive suites pass: hive-brain-recall-quality, agent-memory-routing, agent-memory-upgrade, hive-brain-memory-hardening. Whole-project tsc has no errors outside a concurrently edited companion view. Shared-tree `pnpm test` gate identical before/after: 134/143 with the same nine pre-existing/concurrent reds. The completed 3-replicate claude-sonnet-5 micro-v1 judged panel on the final tree reads LoCoMo 90/90/90, LongMemEval 83.33/66.67/66.67, BEAM 1M 57.25/57.0/59.17, BEAM 10M 52.0/24.75/46.75 — within the measured ±17-point single-rep sampling noise of the pre-change reps in every suite (the 24.75 BEAM 10M rep was integrity-checked: no empty or errored answers, genuine sampling variance), so the judged panel neither certifies nor refutes score movement; the deterministic probes above are the confirmed effects.
  - Rollback: remove `standingGuidanceTurns`, the guidance merge/fallback prefix blocks, and `isAggregationRecallQuery` from excerpt.ts; restore the single-expression hit pipeline in `hitsFromRecords` and remove `recentConversationNoteRecords`/the supplement block in core.ts; restore the four-passage aggregation limit and the previous test file assertions.
  - Intended commit message: `agent-memory: standing-guidance recall channel + aggregation session padding`

- 2026-07-11 03:49:11 +0800 - Windows setup no longer opens a blocking Script Host error
  - Status: Pushed in `45f3216a5`
  - Areas changed: Windows collector and Hivemind Link hidden launchers, Scheduled Task and Startup-folder registration, Windows uninstall cleanup, and the native first-launch regression contract.
  - Summary: Windows setup no longer asks `WScript.Shell.Run` to synchronously wait for the long-running collector or Hivemind Link process, the call that can raise `80020009: Unable to wait for process` in a blocking Windows Script Host dialog and leave the setup modal looking frozen. The installer now writes hidden PowerShell supervisors backed by .NET process handles, keeps each service attached to its supervising task, and returns the child exit code without a visible console. Scheduled Tasks and direct setup starts invoke those supervisors directly; the standard-user Startup-folder fallback keeps only a non-waiting VBS shim. Upgrades remove the legacy blocking VBS launchers and successful task registration removes any stale Startup fallback, while uninstall removes both the new supervisors and old launcher files.
  - Verification: TDD first made `node scripts/test-native-first-launch-privacy.mjs` fail on the old `wscript.exe` action, synchronous `Run(..., True)` call, missing .NET supervisor, and stale Startup fallback; it passes after the change. PowerShell parser checks pass for `scripts/install-telemetry-collector.ps1`, `setup.ps1`, and `uninstall.ps1`. On a clean Vultr Windows Server 2022 VM, the old VBS launcher completed normally over SSH, confirming the reported `80020009` is desktop/environment-sensitive rather than universal. The exact patched app setup path (`setup.ps1 -NonInteractive -SkipDeps -SkipBuild -SkipDashboard`) then bootstrapped Node and Python, exited 0, registered an S4U task whose action is `powershell.exe ... run-collector-hidden.ps1`, stayed `Running` after SSH disconnect, and returned healthy collector JSON on port 8787 with both supervisor and Node child alive. No legacy collector VBS or stale Startup fallback remained. A forced Task Scheduler denial exercised the fallback end to end: its VBS returned 0 immediately, targeted the PowerShell supervisor, contained no synchronous wait, brought port 8799 healthy, and left no legacy VBS. A disposable standard-user password-logon task never launched on this Server image (`0x41303`), so that specific harness path is unverified here. A forced collector-child crash also confirmed a separate pre-existing flaw: Task Scheduler records exit `-1` but does not perform the advertised automatic restart; the task was manually restarted and health restored. The freeze fix does not change that behavior.
  - Rollback: restore the synchronous hidden VBS launchers and point Scheduled Tasks/direct starts back to `wscript.exe`; rerunning the restored installer recreates the old files. No user data or collector configuration format was migrated.
  - Intended commit message: `setup: replace blocking Windows collector VBS launcher`

- 2026-07-11 02:45:22 +0800 - Image-to-video accepts common image formats and honors requested seconds
  - Status: Pushed in `45f3216a5`
  - Areas changed: canonical chat-image format matrix; composer and Tauri desktop preview recognition, server materialization, Media Studio upload naming, follow-up source recovery, and signed source-thumbnail serving; SVG preview sandboxing; Media Studio MCP duration parsing and frame-count construction; focused TypeScript/route and Rust image-format regressions.
  - Summary: Dragged APNG, AVIF, BMP/DIB, GIF, HEIC/HEIF, ICO, JPEG and its common aliases, PNG, SVG, TIFF, and WebP files now follow one shared image contract from the composer through image-to-video generation, iterative follow-ups, and source-thumbnail delivery. This closes the mismatch where the composer recognized more image types than the server and prevents another one-extension omission like `.jpeg`; WebP was already functional and is now locked by the same end-to-end regression. - 2026-07-10 22:40:00 PST+0800 - Deleting a chat thread now also erases its shared-brain conversation mirror (hard delete)
  - Status: Pushed in `45f3216a5`
  - Areas changed: `src/lib/services/obsidian/conversation-notes.ts` (new `deleteConversationNotesForThread`, plus pure `conversationIndexLinesWithoutThread` / `conversationNoteChatStorageKey` / `isPurgeableConversationNotePath`, an atomic index rewrite, and an in-process write chain shared with the existing append); `src/lib/services/obsidian/full-vault-search-index.ts` (new `removeFullVaultSearchIndexPaths` + pure `fullVaultIndexLinesWithoutPaths`; extracted the atomic `writeIndexFileAtomically` helper that `rebuildFullVaultSearchIndex` now reuses); `src/app/api/chat/thread/route.ts` (DELETE also purges the mirror; corrected doc comment); new `scripts/test-chat-thread-vault-purge.mjs` wired into `scripts/test-gate.mjs` + `package.json`; `AGENTS.md` (two new rules)
  - Summary: The 21:55 telemetry purge left the shared-brain mirror behind, so a "deleted" chat stayed recallable by every agent on the fleet. `DELETE /api/chat/thread?chatStorageKey=…` now also removes the thread's `Memory/Conversations/<agent>/*.md` notes, its `Conversations Index.jsonl` rows, and — critically — its rows in the generated `Full Vault Search Index.jsonl`. That last part is not cosmetic: an index row carries the note's `excerpt`, `headings`, `tags`, and full term vector, so leaving it would keep the deleted conversation searchable *and quotable* for up to the 6h index TTL. Notes, not the index, are the source of truth for what is purgeable: `syncConversationNoteForSession` writes the note before appending its row, so a failed append leaves a note no row can address — the purge therefore scans `Memory/Conversations` by frontmatter `chatStorageKey` and unions that with the index rows. Nothing in the app reads `Conversations Index.jsonl` today (only the writer), so its rows are rewritten out rather than tombstoned; a tombstone would have had to retain `title` and `keywords`, both derived from the user's own message, which would leak the substance of the conversation it claims to have deleted. Because the purge is a read-modify-write over a file the note writer appends to, both now funnel through one in-process promise chain (mirroring `serializeTelemetryWrite`), or a concurrent session's row would be silently dropped. **Security:** `notePath` is read back out of a JSONL file that Syncthing replicates from other machines, i.e. untrusted input, and the unlink has no undo — so every path passes `isPurgeableConversationNotePath` (must sit under `Memory/Conversations/`, end in `.md`, contain no `.`/`..`/empty segment), plus a second check on the resolved path. A blank `chatStorageKey` matches nothing: 17 of the 92 notes currently in the vault were written by sessions with an empty key, and a blank-key sweep would have destroyed all of them.
  - Decision + known limits: Liam chose **hard delete, on every thread delete**, over a local-trash variant, having been shown that no rollback path exists. Named honestly: (a) the 17 empty-`chatStorageKey` notes are not thread-addressable and can never be purged this way — that is a pre-existing defect in `startRuntimeChatSession`, which propagates `""` through, and it is *not* fixed here; (b) `finishRuntimeChatSession` fires the note write fire-and-forget, so a session finishing during a purge can re-create its note afterwards; (c) `okf.ts` can bundle `Memory/Conversations` into OKF export bundles, which a purge does not retract (they are regenerable); (d) the write chain is in-process, so a second Next process could still race.
  - Verification: Baseline `pnpm test` **before** any edit was 132/141 with 9 red; **after**, 133/142 with the **same 9 red diffed by name**, and the new `test:chat-thread-vault-purge` PASSing inside the gate (141ms). The `check-sizes` and `guard:hive-action-route-drift` failure bodies are **byte-identical** before and after (diffed), so the new route adds no drift and no file crossed the ratchet. The 9 are pre-existing failures from other sessions' uncommitted work in this shared tree. `pnpm typecheck` exits 0 (real exit code, unpiped). `pnpm lint` exits 1 with 454 pre-existing problems, none in any file I touched. The suite exercises the real `deleteConversationNotesForThread` against a throwaway tmp vault: it asserts the traversal row `Memory/Conversations/../../../sentinel.md` removes its index row but leaves the out-of-vault sentinel on disk, that `/etc/passwd` is refused, that another thread's note and a keyless note survive, that emptied agent folders are pruned while occupied ones are not, that unparseable index lines are preserved, that re-running is idempotent, and that a note with no index row is still purged via its frontmatter. Two findings caught during verification: my first traversal fixture used `../..`, which resolves back to the vault root — the assertion was **vacuous**; it now uses `../../..` and the test asserts `resolve(root, TRAVERSAL) === sentinel` so it can never silently go vacuous again. And a mutation test (guard stubbed to `return true`) turned the suite **red**, confirming the guard is load-bearing rather than decorative; the stub was reverted by hand and `rg` confirms no marker remains. NOT verified: no real thread was deleted and Liam's actual vault was never written to — every test ran against tmp fixtures, and the 92 real notes / 96 index rows are untouched. Only Liam can confirm the click-through, which is irreversible. Fixture dirs are deliberately never named `hivemindos-vault`, because `resolveObsidianVaultPath` treats that suffix (and a missing path) as an auto-detect hint and would have discovered — and purged — the real vault.
  - Rollback (of the code, not of purged notes): revert the four source files and delete `scripts/test-chat-thread-vault-purge.mjs`, unregistering it from `scripts/test-gate.mjs` + `package.json`; in `full-vault-search-index.ts` re-inline `writeIndexFileAtomically` back into `rebuildFullVaultSearchIndex`. Removing the `deleteConversationNotesForThread` call from the route is sufficient to disable the behaviour on its own. **Notes destroyed by a real purge are NOT recoverable**: the vault is not a git repo, its Syncthing folder has file versioning disabled (`<versioning></versioning>`, no `.stversions`), Obsidian's trash does not apply to `fs.unlink`, and the delete replicates fleet-wide within ~10s (`fsWatcherDelayS="10"`). Do NOT bulk `git checkout` this shared tree.
  - Intended commit message: `chat: deleting a thread now erases its shared-vault conversation mirror`

- 2026-07-10 19:41:13 PST+0800 - xAI OAuth refreshes automatically without competing token copies
  - Status: Pushed in `45f3216a5`
  - Areas changed: HivemindOS-owned xAI OAuth store and lock-compatible token broker; optional existing-Hermes authority adapter; app OAuth login/status/access service; cross-platform shared-env retirement helper; embedded Tauri runtime script packaging; xAI OAuth route copy; focused concurrent-rotation, no-Hermes, optional-Hermes, provider setup, and package coverage; `OPTIMIZATIONS.md`.
  - Summary: xAI OAuth sessions are now machine-local rotating credentials rather than fleet-synced static keys. A normal HivemindOS login is owned entirely by `~/.hivemindos/oauth/xai.json` and `xai.lock`; Hermes is not required or created. If a user already signed in through Hermes, one non-secret authority selector can reference that existing `auth.json` in place and the broker participates in its `auth.lock` without copying the refresh token. Either way, one active store owns each rotating grant, so simultaneous requests re-read the winner's newly rotated pair instead of replaying a single-use refresh token. Valid access tokens remain cached in the app process, and refresh is invisible during normal use. Legacy shared-env copies migrate once into the native store and are retired with synced tombstones. A token already revoked before this fix still requires one reconnect.
  - Verification: TDD reproduced the ownership requirement with two independent broker processes against one expired native HivemindOS session; both completed with the same fresh access token, the mock xAI endpoint received exactly one refresh request, and the native store contained the rotated refresh token. The disposable no-Hermes home created `.hivemindos/oauth/xai.json` and no `.hermes/auth.json`, and the real app accessor returned that native token. A separate optional-Hermes case selected a profile store in place, returned its valid access token through a fresh app accessor, and proved its refresh token was neither copied nor rotated. A terminal-grant case makes one failed refresh, quarantines the dead pair, and makes later checks fail locally without another request. Broker, provider-setup and inference-routing contracts, Python/packaging syntax checks, focused zero-warning ESLint, whole-project TypeScript with no emitted diagnostics, and whitespace checks pass. The package contract requires both the broker and `hive-env-add` beside the embedded Next server. Before the ownership correction, the running authenticated status route reported the real revoked state and a live Queen fallback completed in 1.59 seconds; that already-revoked grant remains pending one reconnect.
  - Rollback: restore direct refresh and shared-env token writes in `xai-oauth.ts`, remove the native broker/authority selector/env-removal helper, and restore the previous tests. That would recreate multiple independent owners of one single-use refresh token and is not recommended. The current legacy shared-env values were inspected only for presence and were not deleted during verification; the normal successful reconnect/migration path retires them.
  - Intended commit message: `auth: make xai oauth native and refresh-safe`

  - Rollback: restore the timestamped local dashboard-state backup, restore Ubuntu's collector script from its timestamped pre-deploy backup and restart the user service, then revert only the reserved-profile source/test hunks listed above.
  - Intended commit message: `collector: block reserved probe profiles from fleet snapshots`

- 2026-07-10 12:29:29 PST+0800 - Queen Bee can discover and execute any registered Hive capability without provider-specific prompt wiring
  - Status: Pushed in `45f3216a5`
  - Areas changed: Queen Bee shared tool contract and typed/realtime/Gemini/pipeline executors; full agent capability preflight; generic MCP/connected-app/Hive-Action executor; live MCP schema inventory; MCP annotation preservation; capability telemetry and Tailnet redaction; focused Queen/capability tests; `OPTIMIZATIONS.md`
  - Summary: Queen previously knew about Hive capability search but could execute only a small hardcoded tool set in her direct pipeline, while the full runtime's capability results omitted canonical Hive Action ids. That split let a model see "List HivemindOS machines," guess that it was an MCP tool, list an unrelated empty MCP roster, and confidently report zero. Queen now advertises one provider-neutral `use_hive_capability` meta-tool (the old `ask_hivemind_agent` name remains accepted only as a compatibility alias for already-open clients). Canonical generic requests try the built-in registry executor before configured runtimes, so a conversational runtime cannot intercept them with an unsupported-capability denial; runtime-specific agents remain fallback when the response stream has no real execution or approval receipt. Registry inspection and execution are distinct, so listing an empty catalog cannot masquerade as completed work. The registry runs full capability search, whose hits now include exact executable ids and invocation coordinates. Tool-capable runtimes receive one stable `invoke_hive_capability` function that can inspect or call live in-app MCP tools, connected-app endpoints, and registered Hive Actions. A future social MCP becomes available from its live `tools/list` schema with no Queen prompt edit; a social API becomes available by exposing a connected-app endpoint or a typed Hive Action. Read-only MCP tools, app GETs, and read-only Hive Actions run directly. Unknown/mutating MCP calls and raw app POSTs require Bypass permission, while Hive Actions and annotated MCP tools retain their exact declared confirmation token. External MCP descriptions/schemas are wrapped as untrusted prompt data, and returned Tailnet addresses are redacted before entering model context.
  - Verification: TDD started red because the generic capability modules did not exist. `test-registered-capability-tool`, `test-queen-chat-stream`, and full TypeScript now pass. The focused executor tests cover live-MCP discovery/schema context, read-only MCP execution, blocked and Bypass-approved MCP mutations, connected-app GET execution and POST blocking, canonical/prefixed Hive Action ids, exact public-message confirmation, runtime wiring, registry-first routing, inspection-versus-execution SSE receipts, and Tailnet redaction. A real dashboard invocation executed `fleet.list-machines` through the generic Hive Action path. A model-selected inner-runtime probe first reproduced the missing-id bug, then selected `Hive Action fleet.list-machines` after canonical ids were added; the final evidence-aware inner probe returned `capabilityExecuted=true`. A full Queen pipeline turn with `gpt-4o` chose `use_hive_capability`, the inner runtime completed that Hive Action, and Queen answered from the live receipt in 11.33 s in an isolated home and 13.81 s in the final real-home evidence-aware run, without exposing a Tailnet address. In the isolated outer harness, `gpt-4o-mini` once ignored `tool_choice:auto`; the architecture remains available, but small-model tool compliance is not guaranteed. No third-party social MCP is currently connected, so its actual upstream auth/network call remains unverified; the in-app MCP transport call is covered with a protocol-shaped test double.
  - Intended commit message: `queen: execute arbitrary registered capabilities through one hive registry`

- 2026-07-10 11:44:48 PST+0800 - Shared Brain separates run receipts from durable truth, keeps one canonical head, and review-gates mined patterns
  - Status: Pushed in `45f3216a5`
  - Areas changed: Agent Memory canonical-key/head selection, local operational event journal, recall/health/consolidation behavior, Queen Bee and handoff receipt routing, memory API + `hive-brain` CLI, review-gated operational pattern miner, labeled benchmark and focused regression suites, packaged Shared Brain skill and whole-brain docs/setup contracts
  - Summary: Routine completions and receipts now append to a bounded local operational journal instead of becoming durable Agent Memory notes, and legacy `action` notes are excluded from default recall and duplicate consolidation while remaining explicitly queryable.   - Status: Pushed in `45f3216a5`

  - Summary: The Fleet view's orbital-graph task channel logged a React duplicate-key warning (`Encountered two children with the same key, hermes-state:20260710_015817_7d3e49`) from `orbital-graph.tsx:518` (`tasks.slice(0,12).map(t => … key={t.id})`). Root cause (confirmed by reading the call chain): the snapshot API mints Hermes-session task ids as `hermes-state:<sessionId>` with **no agent prefix** (`src/app/api/fleet/snapshot/route.ts:421`); the same shared `~/.hermes` session therefore surfaces under more than one agent's snapshot. Per-agent work lists are already deduped in `candidateWorkById`, but the graph's `tasks` array is built by `Object.entries(agentWorkById).flatMap(...)` (`use-dashboard-derived-state.tsx:1291`) which flattens **across** agents with no dedupe — so two `FleetTask`s with the same `id` reached the render. - 2026-07-10 03:05:00 PST+0800 - Copy-trading: Base detector now sees native-ETH and token↔token swaps (closed the two blind spots)
  - Status: Pushed in `45f3216a5`
  - Areas changed: `src/lib/services/copy-trading/watcher.ts` (new exported pure `classifyEnrichedEvmSwap` + `EnrichedEvmTx` type; `detectBase` now runs a second `detectEnrichedBaseSwaps` enrichment pass; new `addressHasCode` code-cache helper + `dedupeByTxRef`; header comment rewritten to describe full coverage; `tokenLiquidityUsd` import added), `scripts/test-copy-trading.mjs` (8 new fixture tests), `CHANGELOG.md`
  - Summary: The Base copy-trade watcher previously only detected swaps with a USDC/USDT/WETH ERC-20 leg moving directly through the target's wallet (`classifyEvmSwaps`). Investigation for the user (their 2 configured Base "whales" showed 0 trades over ~50h — confirmed genuinely 0 copyable: one all-airdrops, one dormant) surfaced that essentially all current Base smart-money flow is in exactly the two shapes the detector was blind to: **native-ETH** trades (ETH pseudo-address `0xeee…`, the WETH leg lives inside the router, never touches the EOA) and **token↔token** launchpad rotation through a hub token (e.g. ADS + `0xadf…` repo-named microcaps). Nansen confirmed the Base copyable pool was ~1 wallet (and it was down ~$3.8k). This change fills those gaps so any real swap the target makes is mirrorable. New pure `classifyEnrichedEvmSwap` handles: (1) **native-ETH buy** — target initiated the tx, `tx.value > 0`, exactly one non-quote token in, none out → BUY, sized by `value × ETH price` (excludes airdrops: those have `tx.from ≠ target` and zero value); (2) **token↔token** — both a non-quote token in and out, no quote leg; the deeper-DexScreener-liquidity leg is treated as the pseudo-quote/hub, so rotating INTO the thin leg = BUY, back to the hub = SELL; (3) **native-ETH sell** — target routed exactly one token into a pool contract (recipient has code — separates a swap from a plain transfer to an EOA friend) with nothing back → SELL (sized from the copied position). `detectBase` runs `classifyEvmSwaps` first, then enriches only the leftover no-quote-leg txs with per-tx `getTransaction`/`getCode`/`tokenLiquidityUsd` (bounded to the newest `MAX_ENRICH_PER_POLL=60` per poll; steady-state polls have a handful). Engine unchanged — it already mirrors every signal by buying/selling with USDC regardless of the target's quote asset. Existing ERC-20-quote, airdrop, and quote↔quote behaviors are untouched.
  - Verification: `node --test scripts/test-copy-trading.mjs` → **17/17 pass** (was 9; +8 new fixtures covering ETH-buy priced/unpriced, airdrop-by-third-party guard, token↔token buy & sell direction, ETH-sell into a pool, plain-transfer-to-EOA no-signal, and hard-quote deferral). `tsc --noEmit` clean. In the full `pnpm test` gate `test:copy-trading` passes; the gate's 9 red steps are all pre-existing/concurrent-session breakage unrelated to copy-trading (`check-sizes` trips on `WalletsView.tsx`/`stream-openai-compatible.ts`/`catalog.ts` — my `watcher.ts` is 520 lines; the 7 failing suites are acting-wallet/agent-providers/chat/company/gbrain and none import copy-trading — no clean-tree baseline was captured, but causation is ruled out by file scope). **Real-chain validation** (replayed the exact enrichment algorithm via RPC + DexScreener): native-ETH buys — 8/8 real Base txs classified BUY with the ETH amount matching `tx.value` and the token matching Nansen's record (NOCK/LUNA/OLYN/IONA); token↔token — correct BUY/SELL on real launchpad rotations (incl. the ADS↔SOCIAL-APP tx `0x1da5fad0…`). NOT live-verified: a native-ETH *sell* against a live tx (unit-tested only), and the end-to-end daemon run (detection is `detectNewSwaps`-wired but not exercised inside the running daemon this session; on Liam's network Node/undici to `mainnet.base.org` can ETIMEDOUT while curl succeeds, so a live node-side detectBase run was deliberately not used as the gate).
  - Risk/rollback: false-positive detections would only cause extra dry-run "would buy/sell" log entries for the user's current configs (all `dryRun:true`, $10 cap); revert is `watcher.ts` + the test file only, no engine/state/schema changes. Follow-up worth considering: native-ETH sells currently rely on the recipient-has-code heuristic (a token sent to a non-DEX contract — staking/bridge — could read as a sell, but only acts if we already hold that position).
  - Intended commit message: `copy-trading: detect native-ETH + token↔token swaps on Base`

Location is best-effort: for remote-machine discovery it's the targeted machine's fleet location; for LM Link it matches the device name (possessive/suffix-normalized) to a single non-self fleet machine and borrows its city label, omitting location on ambiguity rather than guessing. - 2026-07-10 01:51:00 PST+0800 - Fix: the chat bubble's down-arrow now actually collapses the Queen chat history
  - Status: Pushed in `45f3216a5`
  - Areas changed: `src/features/queen-voice/QueenBeeVoiceOverlay.tsx` (TranscriptTurns collapse handler), `CHANGELOG.md`
  - Summary: Pressing the down-tail (down-arrow) at the bottom of the app-wide "Message the hive" chat bubble did nothing. The collapse control lives INSIDE the transcript panel, so at click time the pointer is already over the panel — `handlePointerEnter` has latched `transcriptInteractionActive = true`, which keeps `transcriptExpanded` true. The old handler only called `setHistoryMinimized(true)`, whose effect (`!historyMinimized`) is OR-ed with the still-true interaction hold, so the bubble stayed open and the click looked inert. A store-only reset wouldn't have held either: the `selectionchange` listener re-runs `syncInteractionActive()`, which reads `pointerInsideRef.current` (still true) and re-sets the signal. Fix: a new `handleCollapse` in `TranscriptTurns` drops the local pointer/selection latches (`pointerInsideRef`, `pointerSelectingTextRef`, `textSelectionInsideRef`) and clears the shared interaction signal via `onInteractionActiveChange(false)` BEFORE calling `onCollapse()`, so the manual collapse wins and a trailing pointerup/selectionchange can't immediately re-open it.
  - Verification: `node scripts/test-queen-chat-bubble-autopen.mjs` passes (its string-matched contract lines are unchanged). `pnpm typecheck` reports zero errors in the touched file (the only 2 errors are the pre-existing/concurrent `src/lib/services/x-transcript/media-transcribe.ts` Buffer/ArrayBuffer errors, which I did not touch). NOT yet driven live in a browser: the exact hover→click→collapse interaction (requires existing Queen chat turns + precise pointer sequencing) was verified by tracing the render/derived-state chain, not by a live click.
  - Intended commit message: `queen-chat: make the transcript down-tail actually collapse the history`
