Fix 1 — `videoRouteScore` now requires a genuinely video-specific route (`image-to-video`/`img2vid`/`i2v`/`text-to-video`/`generate-video`/`/videos`, or a `video`/`animate`/`.mp4` descriptor), and `appScore` gained a hard **video-signal gate**: without a `video` serviceKind, a real video route, or a video-specific name/description (the `comfyui`/`media`/`creative` keywords were removed), the app scores 0 and `selectVideoApp` filters it — so the dispatcher returns the honest "No connected video generation app…" (reason `no-app`) instead of wasting a run on an image app. An explicit `appId` pin still wins (respect the caller's choice). Fix 2 — the `generation-failed` return path now carries `appId`/`appName`/`machineName`/`serviceKind` (+ discovered `appCount`), and the route logs them on `chat.video_generation.failed`, so the culprit app is visible from the event alone (before this it took reading the saved session JSON to find it).
  - Verification: `node scripts/test-video-app-routing.mjs` PASS (new hermetic suite: image-only Z-Image/ComfyUI app → `appScore 0` and `selectVideoApp […] === null`; video-route / `serviceKind:video` / video-name apps score > 0; a real video app beats the image app in a mixed fleet; an explicit `appId` pin is honored regardless). `pnpm test:wallet-paid-models` still PASS (it asserts source strings I did not touch). `eslint --quiet` clean on both source files + the test. `tsc --noEmit`: **zero** diagnostics in the two files I changed — the only 2 tsc errors are in `src/lib/services/x-transcript/media-transcribe.ts`, an **untracked** concurrent session's work I did not touch (pre-existing red, not my regression). `check-sizes` passes (video-generation.ts 520 → 555 lines, well under the 1500 cap). NOT verified end-to-end through a live agent turn: no video app exists to select, so the honest `no-app` path can't be exercised against a real backend until a video app is connected (fix #1/#3 from the diagnosis). Claim I'd most expect to want a second look at: that no *currently-working* video generation regresses — safe here because the fleet has zero video apps today, so the stricter gate changes only which failure message shows, not any passing path.
  - Follow-up (not built): give the NYC "Media Studio" a REST video endpoint the collector can catalog as `serviceKind: video` (its video capability is currently an MCP tool `media_generate_video`, and `generate_video` is REST-only — no MCP bridge), and fix the stale NYC app-proxy IP in fleet discovery (cache pointed at a dead host).
  - Intended commit message: `video-gen: gate out image-only apps from video routing + record app on failure`

- 2026-07-09 23:18:00 PST+0800 - Chat image attachments render as thumbnails with a FLIP expand-to-lightbox
  - Status: Pushed in `45f3216a5`
  - Areas changed: `src/features/chat/image-attachment-preview.tsx` (new — thumbnail + FLIP lightbox), `src/features/chat/image-attachment-preview.module.css` (new), `src/features/chat/chat-attachment-view.tsx` (new — the single shared attachment renderer + `MessageAttachments`), `src/features/chat/chat-file-references.ts` (image detection + preview hydration), `src/features/chat/chat-formatters.ts` (`attachmentKindLabel`/`attachmentDetailLabel`/`attachmentReferenceTarget` moved here), `src/features/chat/chat-composer.tsx` (tray uses `ChatAttachmentView`; `MessageAttachments` + label/ref helpers moved out; summary counts use `isImageAttachment`; re-exports `MessageAttachments`), `src/features/dashboard/views/chat/exchange/MessageThread.tsx` (`AttachmentPills` uses `ChatAttachmentView`), `src/features/dashboard/hooks/use-status-chat-input-controller.tsx` (drop handler hydrates previews, passes native path reader), `src/lib/types/kanban.ts` (`previewUrl` field), `src/lib/native/local-image.ts` (new — `readLocalImagePreview` invoke), `src-tauri/src/image_preview.rs` (new — `read_local_image_preview` command), `src-tauri/src/lib.rs` (register command), `src-tauri/build.rs` (command list for permission gen), `src-tauri/Cargo.toml` (`base64`), `src-tauri/capabilities/default.json` (`allow-read-local-image-preview`), `CHANGELOG.md`
  - Summary: In the chat route, image attachments render as a small thumbnail instead of the generic "File <name> reference" pill — a 60×60 `object-fit:cover` tile with a corner remove button in the composer tray, and an aspect-preserved ≤240px preview in the sent user bubble. Clicking a thumbnail opens a full-screen lightbox with a FLIP (First-Last-Invert-Play) shared-element transition: the preview grows out of the thumbnail's exact rect and, on close (backdrop / × / Escape), shrinks back into that same size and position before unmounting. The overlay is portaled to `document.body` at `z-index:1200` (above the composer's max of 1000), fades the backdrop, restores focus to the thumbnail, and honors `prefers-reduced-motion` (opacity-only). **Key fix over the first pass:** the reported case (`swarm-scout-card.jpg`) arrives as a path *reference* (`kind:"file"`, `referenceOnly`, empty `dataUrl`) — dropped image bytes are discarded when the reference is created — so a `dataUrl`-only check never matched. Now `isImageAttachment` classifies by kind/mime/extension, and `hydrateImageReferencePreviews` reads a downscaled (≤1024px) **display-only** `previewUrl` from the dropped file's bytes when present (browser drops and the file/image pickers). `previewUrl` is never sent to the agent — `messageContentParts` still sends the path reference, so runtime behavior is unchanged. Desktop native drops give only a path with no bytes (see the next bullet for the native read that handles them). `imageAttachmentPreviewSrc` picks the display source (`previewUrl` → inline `dataUrl`) for both the composer and thread. Non-image attachments keep the pill.
  - Desktop native drop (the reported case, 2026-07-10): on the Tauri desktop app the OS drop is swallowed and the webview gets **only the file path — zero bytes** (`filesFromReferencePaths` builds `new File([])`), so the bytes-based hydration does nothing and the pill persists. Added a native command `read_local_image_preview(path)` (`src-tauri/src/image_preview.rs`; base64 data URL, image-extension-gated, 25 MB cap), exposed via `readLocalImagePreview` (`src/lib/native/local-image.ts`, desktop-only guard). `hydrateImageReferencePreviews` now takes an optional path reader: a dropped image reference with no bytes but a `referencePath` is read natively → downscaled to `previewUrl`. Works in dev and packaged/static desktop (native invoke, not an `/api` route); off-desktop the reader is null and the browser path is unchanged. The command's permission is generated from the explicit command list in `src-tauri/build.rs` (not the handler) — a missing entry there **fails the build**, which is exactly what `cargo check` caught before this reached you.
  - Single source of truth (follow-up on request): all attachment rendering now flows through one component, `ChatAttachmentView(surface: "composer" | "message" | "gallery")` in `chat-attachment-view.tsx`. It uses the one image check (`imageAttachmentPreviewSrc`/`isImageAttachment`) and the one thumbnail (`ImageAttachmentThumbnail`) across the composer tray, the sent chat thread (`AttachmentPills`), and the Kanban message list (`MessageAttachments`, now a thin wrapper — so Kanban images become clickable lightbox thumbnails too instead of plain `<img>`). The old per-surface branches (`ComposerAttachmentItem`, the inline thread branch, the `MessageAttachments` image `<img>`) and their scattered `attachment.kind === "image"` checks are gone; the composer attachment-count summary also routes through `isImageAttachment`. Deliberately left separate: `messageContentParts` still gates the **runtime payload** on `kind === "image"` (image references never reach it — they're caught earlier by the no-`dataUrl` branch), so display consolidation never changes what the agent receives. Net effect on the size ratchet: `chat-composer.tsx` dropped to 1453 lines (below its HEAD baseline).
  - Verification: full `pnpm typecheck` clean; `eslint --quiet` clean on all touched files. Pure classification logic (`isImageAttachment`, `imageAttachmentPreviewSrc`) unit-tested against the real source — 9/9 cases incl. the exact `swarm-scout-card.jpg` reference (pill before hydration → thumbnail after). The runtime pipeline was verified in a real Chromium via a harness running the **verbatim** `createFileReferenceAttachment` + `generateImagePreviewDataUrl` + `hydrateImageReferencePreviews` code against a real 26 KB image `File`: the reference first renders as the pill, then the canvas produces a 17 KB image data URL and it swaps to a thumbnail that expands/collapses via the FLIP. `pnpm check-sizes`: none of my files are a new violation (chat-composer under 1500; the controller stays within its 1660 allowance for my ~6 lines). After the single-source consolidation, `pnpm typecheck` + `eslint` + the 9/9 classification test were re-run green and `chat-composer.tsx` measured 1453 (below its HEAD baseline). NOT verified against the live React component in the running app: the auth-gated dashboard would not hydrate in a second Turbopack dev server on this shared repo dir (and a concurrent session now holds the single Next-dev slot), so the fresh full-surface (`ChatAttachmentView` composer/message/gallery) render is the user's check. The image path itself (`ImageAttachmentThumbnail`) was browser-verified in earlier turns; the unified renderer routes to it, and the non-image fallbacks are verbatim ports of the prior renderers. User's final check: drop/upload an image in chat, confirm the composer thumbnail, expand/collapse, send, confirm the in-thread thumbnail (and a Kanban message image is now a clickable thumbnail). The native desktop read was compile-checked: `cargo check` in `src-tauri` is clean after adding the command to `build.rs`'s permission list (the first check failed with "Permission allow-read-local-image-preview not found" — caught before shipping). **NOT verified at runtime in the desktop app:** I can't drive the Tauri window or safely rebuild it from here, so the actual desktop drop→thumbnail is your test — run/restart `pnpm tauri:dev` (or let its watcher rebuild) and drop `swarm-scout-card.jpg`; it should now render a thumbnail. Remaining limits: browser-undecodable formats (e.g. HEIC in Chromium) fall back to the pill by design; only the chat composer drop is wired for the native path read (Kanban/quick-add composers still pill on native drop). Rollback: revert the four `src-tauri/*` edits + `src/lib/native/local-image.ts` and drop the 4th arg to `hydrateImageReferencePreviews`.
  - Note: the full `pnpm test`/`check-sizes` gate is currently red from ~15 files inflated by *other* concurrent uncommitted sessions (e.g. `WalletsView.tsx` 2072/1850, `stream-openai-compatible.ts` 1840, `nansen.ts` 1640) — not from this change; left untouched per the shared-tree rule.
  - Intended commit message: `chat: render image attachments (incl. dropped references) as thumbnails with a FLIP lightbox`

  - Status: Pushed in `45f3216a5`
  - Areas changed (app, this repo): `src/lib/services/integrations/slack-oauth.ts` (rewritten to the broker+poll model), `src/app/api/integrations/slack/oauth/start/route.ts` (returns `flowId`), `src/app/api/integrations/slack/oauth/poll/route.ts` (new), `src/app/api/integrations/slack/oauth/callback/route.ts` (**deleted** — redirect now lands on the Worker), `src/proxy.ts` (slack callback entry **reverted** from `SELF_AUTHENTICATING_API_PREFIXES` — no longer an app route), `src/features/integrations/ConnectionsPanel.tsx` (Slack poll loop), `src/lib/services/integrations/{connector-manifests.ts,provider-connection-env.ts,provider-connections.ts}`, `src/lib/types/integrations.ts`, `INTEGRATIONS.md` (rewritten), `AGENTS.md`, `WORKERS.local.md` (new, gitignored), `.gitignore`, `CHANGELOG.md`
  - Areas changed (Worker, PRIVATE `hivemind-cloud-services` repo — not committed here): `workers/google-oauth-exchange/src/index.ts` (+`/slack/start`, `/slack/callback`, `/slack/result` broker routes + KV rendezvous; Google `/token`/`/refresh` untouched), `workers/google-oauth-exchange/wrangler.toml` (KV binding + `SLACK_CLIENT_SECRET` note).
  - Summary: The Slack tile is now a one-click **Connect with Slack** browser sign-in (no pasted `xoxb-` token). Because HivemindOS is a **downloaded desktop app**, the flow uses a **confidential-client broker**, not a localhost/PKCE flow: the client **secret lives only in the hosted Cloudflare Worker** (`hivemindos-google-oauth-exchange`, reused as the shared OAuth broker) — never in the binary or this MIT repo. Slack requires an HTTPS exact-match redirect (no loopback-port wildcard, unlike Google desktop clients), so the redirect lands on the Worker's stable `/slack/callback`; the Worker exchanges the code **with** the secret and hands the `xoxp-` user token back to the originating app instance through a **KV rendezvous** proven by a `poll_secret` (which never traverses the browser/Slack; the token never appears in any URL). The token is stored in the existing `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` hive-env key (send path + `auth.test` verifier unchanged). Public client id `11552592014514.11552619377954` stays baked in (`SLACK_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID_DEFAULT`, env override `SLACK_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`); broker URL override `SLACK_OAUTH_BROKER_URL`. Connector auth mode `oauth-user-token`.
  - Why the pivot (journey, for the record): first built the Google-Cloud-style localhost/PKCE flow. Live testing exposed that it only worked on hand-registered dev ports — a downloaded user's random localhost port is never registrable (Slack `redirect_uri did not match…`), and marking the app a PKCE **public** client to drop the secret is a one-way switch and wrong for a distributed app (`bad_client_secret` until then). Liam's call: hold the secret in Cloudflare like the Google connector. So the localhost callback + its proxy-allowlist entry were removed and replaced with the broker.
  - DEPLOYED + verified live (2026-07-09): KV namespace `OAUTH_RENDEZVOUS` created (`84225c8e…`) and bound; both secrets present (`wrangler secret list` shows `GOOGLE_CLOUD_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` + `SLACK_CLIENT_SECRET`); Worker deployed (version `f518c7d8`). Live smoke against the deployed Worker passed end-to-end: `/slack/start`→`ok`, `/slack/result` with a wrong secret→`403 forbidden` (ownership gate), right secret pre-callback→`pending`, `/slack/callback` renders its page + records state, post-callback poll→`error:no_code` with one-time delete, and Google `/token`→`400 missing-fields` (Google route intact, its secret still set). Earlier symptom: the app's `/slack/start` returned the OLD worker's `Not found. Use POST /token or POST /refresh.` 404 — root cause was simply that the new code had not been deployed; deploying fixed it.
  - Bug fixed this pass — "The Slack sign-in expired" on return: `slack-oauth.ts` kept the per-flow `poll_secret` in a module-level `Map`, which Next dev wipes on recompile (this shared tree has heavy HMR churn) and does not reliably share across the separate `/start` and `/poll` route modules — so the poll found no pending flow and reported expired. Replaced with a small file-backed store at `~/.hivemindos/slack-oauth-pending.json` (0600, TTL-pruned), shared across routes and surviving HMR.
  - Slack app config (Liam): redirect URL set to the Worker `…/slack/callback`; user scope `chat:write`; PKCE left off.
  - Verification: `pnpm typecheck` clean (exit 0); full `pnpm test` gate 106/115 = the exact 9-red baseline (no new regressions) as of the pre-file-store state; drift guard does not flag the slack routes. The **app-side start→poll round-trip and the final live Connect→Connected** are NOT empirically run this pass (couldn't hit the authed routes without commandeering Liam's :5121 or standing up a `.next`-conflicting server) — the file-store fix is typecheck-clean and sound by construction; Liam's retry is the real test.
  - Intended commit message: `integrations: connect slack via oauth broker (secret in cloudflare) like google cloud`

  - Status: Pushed in `45f3216a5`
  - Areas changed: `src/app/api/chat/agent-runtime/{media-artifacts.ts,media-tool-routing.ts,messages.ts,process-events.ts,route.ts,route-telemetry.ts,stream-http-runtime.ts,stream-openai-compatible.ts}`, `src/app/api/chat/{video-generation/route.ts,generated-media/route.ts}`, `src/lib/services/chat/{video-generation.ts,task-retrieval-context.ts}`, `src/features/chat/chat-composer.tsx`, `src/features/dashboard/{chat-generated-media.ts,hooks/status-chat-input-helpers.ts,hooks/status-chat-process-image-generation.ts,hooks/use-status-chat-input-controller.tsx,views/chat/exchange/MessageThread.tsx}`, companion private gateway `workers/paid-agent-gateway/{src/free-models.ts,README.md,test/free-model-status-static.mjs}`, `scripts/test-wallet-paid-models.mjs`, `CHANGELOG.md`
  - Summary: Swarm Sovereign Scout no longer reduces attached images to a text summary for media tasks, and it is not treated as text-only for normal visual Q&A. The dashboard now sends current-turn attachment metadata to the chat runtime, the server materializes inline media into local artifact files, and local image reference attachments are read into native multimodal `image_url` payloads before Scout sees the turn. For ordinary prompts like “what do you think of this?” or “what’s in this image?”, the model-bound prompt strips `Attached file references` path text so Scout does not interpret `/Users/.../screenshots/` as the user’s question. Previous-turn attachments are also converted to text-only filename/type references so old screenshots cannot be mistaken for “this image.” Current-turn attachments are no longer duplicated as base64 in both `attachments` and `messages`, and image attachments are no longer downsampled into 24 KiB JPEG vision copies: Scout receives the actual image bytes that were attached or referenced. The hosted free Scout gateway no longer imposes its old 200k-character Worker body cap by default; `SWARM_SCOUT_FREE_MAX_BODY_CHARS` is now an optional positive override only, leaving ordinary multimodal request size to Cloudflare and the upstream Modal app. The chat runtime also removes the earlier compact Free Scout preflight path, so Scout keeps normal capability retrieval, shared-brain, vault, wallet, and previous-turn context instead of using a reduced prompt for simple media inspection. Hive capability search preflight now creates one canonical runtime process event that is persisted for reload/history and serialized to live SSE for the process panel, so fast Scout answers show the capability-search step without maintaining parallel event shapes. Capability-search discovery text that mentions `image_gen` no longer starts a fake Image generation card, and already-persisted running cards with non-generation prompts such as “what does this image say?” are hidden; the dashboard waits for actual generation events or tool activity before rendering the running card. Video attachments keep their real artifact path but expose a model-visible JPEG preview frame, so a normal “what’s this?” prompt with a `.mov` gives Scout visual input instead of raw video bytes or no visual input. Native image-inspection turns suppress the local `run_command` tool even when the image arrives as a prepared artifact path, so Scout does not try to `ls`, grep, Python, `identify`, or base64-encode an attachment instead of looking at it. Screenshot and error-card text is now framed as visual content, so Scout should say what the screenshot shows instead of turning visible setup copy such as `XAI_API_KEY is missing` into a live configuration claim. Video prompts still get a `generate_video` tool that passes the prepared image path/bytes to connected video-generation apps, generated video files can stream back into the existing video card, and arbitrary local image-path previews are labeled as image files instead of “Generated image.”
  - Verification: `node scripts/test-wallet-paid-models.mjs`, focused `./node_modules/.bin/eslint --quiet` on touched chat/media files, full `./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit --pretty false --skipLibCheck --incremental false`, focused `git diff --check`, and a direct materialization smoke that wrote a fake image attachment to `~/.hivemindos/cache/chat-attachments`, verified the file existed, verified the video-tool Scout-bound message contained the artifact path, and verified it did not include the base64 payload passed. - 2026-07-08 15:44 PST - Hive Compute marketplace inference routing and spare-GPU worker setup
  - Status: Pushed in `45f3216a5`
  - Areas changed: `src/lib/config/hive-compute-marketplace.ts` (new), `src/lib/types/hive-compute-marketplace.ts` (new), `src/lib/services/hive-compute-marketplace.ts` (new), `src/app/api/hive-compute/{marketplace,chat/completions}/route.ts` (new), `src/lib/config/model-provider-gateways.ts`, `src/lib/services/runtime-integrations.ts`, `src/app/api/chat/agent-runtime/{stream-http-runtime,stream-openai-compatible}.ts`, `src/features/dashboard/{DashboardApp.tsx,MorePanel.tsx,dashboard-navigation.ts,dashboard-types.ts,dashboard-light-helpers.tsx,lazy-components.tsx}`, `src/components/fleet-hive/AppNavShelf.tsx`, `src/features/dashboard/views/HiveComputePanel.tsx` (new), `src/features/dashboard/views/HiveComputePanel.module.css` (new), `src/lib/services/context-index.ts`, `docs/for-users/features/{index,runtimes-and-chat,hive-compute}.md`, `workers/README.md`, `scripts/test-hive-compute-marketplace.mjs` (new), `CHANGELOG.md`
  - Summary: HivemindOS now has a first-class **Hive Compute** marketplace provider and dashboard setup surface. Agents can select `Hive Compute` in the model picker, and chat routes through the local `/api/hive-compute/chat/completions` proxy to a configured official or self-hosted OpenAI-compatible gateway. - 2026-07-08 14:20 PST +0800 - Collector/telemetry URLs are host-allowlisted before server-side fetch (SSRF hardening)
  - Status: Pushed in `45f3216a5`
  - Areas changed: `src/lib/services/local-collector-url.ts`, `src/lib/services/messaging/channels.ts`, `src/lib/services/messaging/senders.ts`, `src/app/api/fleet/shell/shell-target.ts`, `src/app/api/machines/directories/route.ts`, `src/app/api/fleet/snapshot/route.ts`, `src/app/api/runtimes/state-sync/route.ts`, `scripts/test-collector-ssrf-guard.mjs` (new), `package.json`, `scripts/test-gate.mjs`, `CHANGELOG.md`
  - Summary: Defense-in-depth against an SSRF-adjacent pattern where several dashboard API routes fetched a client-supplied `telemetryUrl`/collector URL server-side with no host allowlist, letting an authenticated caller make the server POST arbitrary JSON to any host (cloud metadata, RFC-1918 LAN, etc.). One shared helper — `isFleetCollectorUrl` / `assertFleetCollectorUrl` in `local-collector-url.ts` — now validates a collector URL against the trusted fleet surface (loopback, this machine's own interfaces, a Tailscale node via `100.64.0.0/10` / `fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48` / `*.ts.net`, or an mDNS `*.local` host) and rejects everything else before any fetch treats the URL as remote-fetchable. The remote-fetch sites are routed through it: Hermes messaging-channel discovery and bridged sends, remote directory browsing (guards both the HTTP fetch and the Tailscale-SSH fallback), fleet snapshot probes, the runtime state-sync toggle, and `shellBaseFromCollectorUrl` (the single chokepoint for the shell/shell-stream/send-file/cron/TTS-probe fetches). The local-collector fast path is unchanged (loopback/self stays allowed). The routes were already dashboard-auth-gated and Link peer hops remain gated by linkd's owner/tailnet ACL; this is belt-and-suspenders. Pre-existing SSRF, not introduced by the messaging-channels rebuild.
  - Verification: `node scripts/test-collector-ssrf-guard.mjs` (new hermetic suite: non-fleet hosts — metadata, RFC-1918, public IPs, CGNAT boundary, wrong scheme, bare hostnames — rejected; fleet hosts accepted; `shellBaseFromCollectorUrl` funnels through the guard), `node scripts/test-messaging-channels-bridge.mjs` (affected caller, still green), `pnpm typecheck` (exit 0), and full `pnpm test` gate ran the new suite green. The gate reports 5 pre-existing red steps (`check-sizes`, `guard:hive-action-route-drift`, `test:acting-wallet-context`, `test:agent-providers`, `test:company-autonomy`) — all in concurrently-modified files I did not touch (wallet/provider/company/models routes); none reference collector-URL code.
  - Intended commit message: `security: host-allowlist collector URLs before server-side fetch`

- 2026-07-07 23:07 PST +0800 - Shared env self-heals keys that were written without a sync timestamp
  - Status: Pushed in `45f3216a5`
  - Areas changed: `scripts/hive-env-add`, `scripts/test-env-sync-queue.mjs`, `CHANGELOG.md`
  - Summary: A shared-hive-env key could land in `~/.hivemindos/.env` with no per-key `updatedAt` entry in `.env.meta.json` whenever something wrote it outside the sanctioned `apply_update` path (a raw file edit, an out-of-repo tool, an older writer). `pull_reconcile` then reads that key's age as `0.0`, treats it as `UnknownAge`, and refuses to overwrite it (`hive-env-add:1591-1594`), while `export_json` serves it with `updatedAt=0` (`:1719`) so peers won't adopt it either — the key is frozen out of sync in BOTH directions and silently, permanently diverges the moment anyone edits it on one machine. It only looks fine while every machine holds the identical value (the equal-value short-circuit at `:1587-1588`). New self-healing step: `backfill_missing_meta()` stamps any key present in the env file but absent from meta, run FIRST inside `--sync-maintenance` (so the stamped keys take part in the same cycle's pull/push) and exposed as a standalone `--backfill-meta [--dry-run]`. It only fills gaps — never rewrites an existing stamp, never resurrects a tombstone (removed keys keep their meta entry and are absent from the values), never touches values. Kill switch `HIVE_ENV_BACKFILL_META=0`. This is the durable root fix so no key can strand however it was written, replacing a one-off manual re-stamp. Live This Mac audit found 22 real unstamped keys (AGENTMAIL_API_KEY, CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN, GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY, CAL_API_KEY, …) all in this freeze trap; a fleet hash-compare confirmed their values are byte-identical on This Mac, NYC, and hel1-2, so the backfill converges the missing stamps with zero value churn.
  - Verification: `node scripts/test-env-sync-queue.mjs` passes, including new scenario 9 which proves the before/after — with `HIVE_ENV_BACKFILL_META=0` an unstamped key IS reported in `pull.skippedUnknownAge` and stays unstamped; with the backfill on it is stamped, is NO LONGER in `skippedUnknownAge`, and gains a real numeric meta timestamp; a second `--backfill-meta` is idempotent (keeps the original stamp). `python3 -c ast.parse` confirms the script parses; `--help` shows the new flag. A read-only `--backfill-meta --dry-run` against the real env reported the 22 gap keys (OUTREACH_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS is NOT among them — it has been stamped since 2026-07-02). Not yet applied to the live env: This Mac's collector will run the new backfill on its next `--sync-maintenance` cycle (the `~/.local/bin/hive-env-add` wrapper execs this checkout, so the change is live locally); hel1-2/NYC get it after they `git pull`. Kill switch and dry-run verified; no value was read, printed, or mutated.
  - Intended commit message: `hive-env: self-heal keys written without a sync timestamp`

  - Status: Pushed in `45f3216a5`
  - Areas changed: `src/lib/types/company.ts`, `src/lib/services/companies-store.ts`, `src/lib/services/company-autonomy-driver.ts`, `src/app/api/companies/route.ts`, `src/features/dashboard/views/zero-human-companies/Modals.tsx`, `src/features/dashboard/views/zero-human-companies/types.ts`, `src/features/dashboard/views/zero-human-companies/mappers.ts`, `src/features/dashboard/views/zero-human-companies/ZeroHumanCompaniesView.tsx`, `scripts/test-company-autonomy.mjs`, `CHANGELOG.md` (plus a data change: WEBS's company definition in the shared vault)
  - Summary: A Zero Human Company can now auto-pause its own autonomy driver when too many items are already waiting on a human, so the Needs You lane can't silently pile up to hundreds of unreviewed approvals. New optional per-company config `autonomyPause` (`maxWaitingOnHuman`, `countMode` "all" | "deliverable-kinds", `deliverableKinds`): once the count of the company's `needs-human` tasks reaches the threshold, the driver stops planning NEW work and fires one low-severity, in-app, per-company "N waiting on you" nudge. It is fully reversible and self-resuming — in-flight work still finishes, and dispatch restarts on the next tick once the human clears enough to drop back under the threshold (no Stop button, no `frozen` kill switch). Default `countMode` is "all" (every waiting item); "deliverable-kinds" counts only `needs-human` tasks carrying a deliverable of a chosen kind (e.g. just website approvals), and an empty kind list safely falls back to counting all so a mode can never silently count zero. Config is persisted through the replicated company definition and settable via `POST /api/companies` (`action: "upsert"`, `autonomyPause`) or the new per-company control in the Zero Human Companies company-edit modal (Treasury · Governance section: an "Auto-pause at" threshold, a "Count which waiting items" select, and deliverable-kind toggle chips shown when the deliverable-kinds mode is chosen). Re-notify cadence is `HIVEMINDOS_COMPANY_PAUSE_NUDGE_TTL_MS` (default 6h).
  - Verification: Backend verified in isolation against a clean-HEAD `git worktree` (the live working tree carries unrelated concurrent-session changes to the kanban/deliverable path that make one pre-existing deliverable-extraction assertion fail — reproduced by baselining clean HEAD: `company autonomy suite passed`, EXIT 0). My source + my new tests on that clean worktree: `company autonomy suite passed`, EXIT 0. New hermetic coverage in `scripts/test-company-autonomy.mjs` exercises `countCompanyWaitingOnHuman` for all-mode counting, deliverable-kinds filtering, empty-kinds fallback-to-all, status exclusion (only `needs-human` counts), and cross-company isolation — all pass. - 2026-07-07 19:07 PST +0800 - OpenAI voice Preview no longer fails with "Invalid URL (POST /v1/audio/speech)"
  - Status: Pushed in `45f3216a5`
  - Areas changed: `src/lib/services/phone/cloud-voice-transports.ts`, `CHANGELOG.md`
  - Summary: The Calls-panel voice Preview button hit `POST https://api.openai.com/v1/audio/speech` with whatever model the selected runtime transport used. When the selected runtime was the OpenAI realtime hybrid (the default for legacy/unknown voice profiles), that model was `gpt-realtime` — a realtime model the TTS-only speech endpoint rejects with the misleading `Invalid URL (POST /v1/audio/speech)` error. `synthesizeVoicePreview` only fell back to a TTS model when the passed model was empty, so the non-empty realtime id sailed through and failed. The preview now coerces any model outside the TTS-capable set (`gpt-4o-mini-tts`, `tts-1`, `tts-1-hd`) to `gpt-4o-mini-tts`, so previewing an OpenAI voice works regardless of which runtime kind (realtime hybrid or cloud TTS) is selected. Explicit valid TTS model overrides are preserved.
  - Verification: Reproduced the exact user error against the live OpenAI API by POSTing `model:"gpt-realtime"` to `/v1/audio/speech` — returned HTTP 404 with the byte-identical `{ "detail": {...}, "error": {...} }` "Invalid URL" body. After the fix, a script mirroring the edited coercion + fetch returned HTTP 200 with real PCM audio for the previously-failing inputs (`gpt-realtime`→`gpt-4o-mini-tts` with voices `alloy`/`verse`), and preserved explicit `tts-1`. Confirmed the OpenAI realtime-only voices `cedar`/`marin` render fine on `gpt-4o-mini-tts`. `pnpm typecheck` (tsc --noEmit) exited 0. Not verified through the running dashboard UI (the /api surface is auth-gated and the change was proven against the real upstream endpoint instead).

  - Summary: New typed "Deliverable Acceptance Contracts" registry — a capability matrix keyed by deliverable KIND (restaurant website preview, generic web page, outreach email) — defines, platform-wide, what makes an outward deliverable real vs. a placeholder/wireframe skeleton, generalizing the 2026-07-07 failure where a restaurant preview shipped to a live prospect with fake "menu" items ("Menu / offer clarity"), no prices, an empty menu category, and a single stock hero. A pure, dependency-injected orchestrator fetches the customer-facing URL(s) a worker/email presents and runs the matching contract; an affirmative rejection is a HARD-fail receipt that blocks loop completion (→ needs-human), exactly like the existing live-URL integrity gate, so this covers EVERY company that completes work through the Queen Bee autonomous-worker path — not just one company. A second enforcement point in the company email-QA scan flags any live preview/offer link in sent outreach whose page fails its acceptance contract. Fail-closed on affirmative rejection ONLY: unfetchable, reserved/mock, transactional (/paid,/checkout,/book), or ambiguous content abstains and never blocks, so the gate never cries wolf. Kill-switch `QUEEN_BEE_DELIVERABLE_ACCEPTANCE=0`. Hardened after an adversarial multi-agent review of the diff (14 findings triaged, 7 acted on): dropped a standalone "too-thin menu" rule and a "missing-imagery" rule (both false-positive vectors on legit small/plain menus); the wireframe-label rule now needs a MAJORITY of items (one oddly-named real dish can't fail a good menu); the generic near-empty check defers to the restaurant contract and requires no media; and the content-URL shape was unified with the live-URL gate's deploy hosts (.onrender/.fly/.firebaseapp) so coverage doesn't diverge, with deliverables fetched concurrently under a cap of 6.
  - Verification: `node scripts/test-deliverable-acceptance.mjs` passed (13 groups: contracts reject Giuseppe HTML + JSON config; pass a real priced menu, a small/tasting menu, an 8-item menu with one wireframe-ish dish name, and an image-driven splash; don't false-fail a real non-restaurant page; catch lorem-ipsum/near-empty/unfilled-merge-field; orchestrator fails closed on affirmative rejection only, doesn't fetch reserved/transactional URLs, and DOES catch a deploy-host (fly.dev) preview; and the loop-runner emits a hard-fail receipt that `loopCompletionBlock` blocks while a real menu passes). Full gate `pnpm test`: baseline 97/100 (3 pre-existing red from concurrent uncommitted work: `check-sizes`, `guard:hive-action-route-drift`, `test:agent-providers`) → after 98/101 with the SAME 3 red and the new `test:deliverable-acceptance` passing (no regressions; typecheck + eslint green). `eslint --max-warnings=0` on all touched files passed. NOT runtime-verified against a live fleet pickup or a real send — blocking behavior is proven via the `runLoopGates`+`loopCompletionBlock` unit path using Giuseppe's real config/markup shapes, not observed in a running company driver.

(1) A machine's hostname churn (the NYC MacBook wore ≥5 hostnames) minted a fresh per-machine schedule id for the SAME underlying cron, so the dashboard accumulated one enabled "copy" per dead identity (5 "Mac memory pressure watchdog" rows, all sharing underlying Hermes job `567853dca5a5`; 2 "Daily Hive Pulse — Base & AI Agents"). New pure `scheduleLoopSignature`/`dedupeSchedulesByLoop` collapse forks by (runtime + underlying job id + normalized name), keeping the live (freshest-updated) row and carrying the newest run stamp forward; wired into both the runtime-import and shared-vault-merge paths so existing forks collapse on next refresh and future renames can't re-fork. (2) "enabled but no recorded runs / may be silently dead" fired on jobs that demonstrably run (memory-pressure watchdog → Telegram for weeks; Daily Hive Pulse → ran daily) because `lastRunAt` was never persisted: `schedulerSharedSnapshot` omitted it so every shared-vault round-trip dropped it, and the Hermes adapter only reported the coarse `jobs.json` file mtime. Now the snapshot serializes/deserializes `lastRunAt`/`lastStatus`/`lastSummary`, the merge keeps the newest run stamp, and the Hermes adapter surfaces each job's real `last_run_at` from `jobs.json`. Residual (named, not fixed): remote schedules imported via a collector `/schedules` still depend on that collector (the Go `linkd`/collector binary, out of this repo) reporting `last_run_at`.

  - Status: Pushed in `45f3216a5` — code change only; not observed live (needs the running dashboard on a company with sent mail, e.g. WEBS)
  - Areas changed: `src/features/dashboard/views/zero-human-companies/EmailQaBand.tsx` (new `EmailQaLoadingCard` shape-matched shimmer + `Skeleton` import; render tail reworked around a `mayYieldMore = deepLoading && report !== null && report.emailCount > 0` gate)
  - Why: Liam reported the Issues screen "starts empty, 2 issues pop in, then 5-10s later the rest pop in." Traced through the code: `IssuesPanel` composes three async sources — the kanban review-issue cards (already skeleton-gated by `initialTasksLoading`), `SetupBlockerBand` (fast local env check), and `EmailQaBand`, which fires TWO requests: a fast deterministic GET then a slow deep-AI POST (`{ deep: true }`). The deterministic findings render immediately (the "2"); the AI findings land 5-10s later (the "3") with NO loading placeholder — the only prior indicator was a header spinner and a text line that showed just for clean companies. The 5-10s latency is the LLM content review (the one source in this panel with that signature — SetupBlockerBand and the kanban issues both land fast/atomically), so this band was the last uncovered wave. The "badge shows 5 but 2 cards" part is separate and by design: the tab badge counts `activeIssueCount` (all non-done kanban issues) while the panel body shows the needs-you subset + these bands.
  - Fix: when we KNOW the company has sent mail (`report.emailCount > 0`) and the AI pass is still running, render a shape-matched skeleton card — as a trailing placeholder below the deterministic findings, or as the whole band's content when the deterministic pass was clean. Gated on `emailCount > 0` so companies with no email crew never flash an email-QA skeleton (and it also fixes a pre-existing minor bug where the old "Reviewing sent emails…" line showed for 5-10s even on companies that never sent email). `SetupBlockerBand` deliberately left alone — its fetch is fast and additive-empty in the common case, so a skeleton there would flash-then-vanish on every company (net negative).
  - Verification: `tsc --noEmit` exit 0 (whole-project, contention-free run — clean); `eslint` exit 0 on `EmailQaBand.tsx`. NOT verified live — the transient AI-review window needs the running dashboard on a company with sent mail; the dev server won't stabilize under the current concurrent-session churn. The one claim I'd most expect to need a live check: that on WEBS the trailing skeleton actually bridges the deterministic→AI gap rather than flashing.

- 2026-07-06 20:05 +0800 - Shared-env sync now self-heals strands: periodic maintenance PUSHES keys a peer is missing, not just pulls (root-cause fix for "should be automatic") — IN-REPO, NOT DEPLOYED
  - Status: Pushed in `45f3216a5` (needs a per-machine-key audit + fleet deploy — see below — before it goes live)
  - Areas changed: `scripts/hive-env-add` (new `push_missing_reconcile` + `push_missing_enabled`; wired into `--sync-maintenance` AFTER pull_reconcile; new standalone `--push-missing [--dry-run]` flag), `scripts/test-env-sync-queue.mjs` (new push-missing scenarios: seeds a key the peer entirely lacks, NEVER clobbers a value the peer already holds, honors the `HIVE_ENV_PUSH_MISSING=0` kill switch, and asserts `--sync-maintenance` reports the push phase).
  - Root cause (confirmed live 2026-07-06): the collector's periodic `hive-env-add --sync-maintenance` (every 10 min) only retried failed writes and PULLED newer keys from peers. It never proactively PUSHED healthy local keys to peers that lack them (that only happened at write-time and in the manual `--reconcile`). Combined with asymmetric reachability — `PORTFOLIO_OFFER_API_TOKEN` lived ONLY on This Mac (a laptop the hel1-2 VPS can't dial inbound), and This Mac (which CAN dial hel1-2 and HAS the key) only ever pulled — the key stranded permanently and silently (all collectors reported `lastError: null`; hel1-2 served 100 keys vs This Mac's 119). Verified: This Mac serves the token via `/env`; hel1-2 and NYC do not.
  - The fix: after pulling, `--sync-maintenance` now seeds each reachable peer with ONLY the keys it is entirely missing. Missing-only is the safety property — it never overwrites a value the peer already holds, so it cannot clobber a newer copy or ping-pong (the receiver stamps pushed keys as now/last-writer-wins, which is why a blind full-push is unsafe — that was the 2026-07-05 clobber incident). Kill switch `HIVE_ENV_PUSH_MISSING=0`. Known residual: a key deleted on a peer during a partition but still live locally could be re-seeded once; rare + self-correcting; the complete fix is receiver-side timestamp/tombstone honoring on the `/env` POST ingest (follow-up).
  - Verification: `test-env-sync-queue` green with the new scenarios; `test-hive-env-roundtrip` green; `python3 -m ast` parse clean; `--help` OK. LIVE DRY-RUN against the real fleet (`--push-missing --dry-run`, zero writes/pushes) confirms it would seed hel1-2 with 21 missing keys INCLUDING `PORTFOLIO_OFFER_API_TOKEN` (and NYC with 6) — healing the exact strand that blocked the two send cards — and correctly does NOT re-push `AGENTMAIL_API_KEY` (hel1-2 already has it).
  - ⚠ CORRECTION (2026-07-06 21:10): my "NO live effect until deployed" claim above was WRONG. `~/.local/bin/hive-env-add` is an 844-byte WRAPPER that `exec`s the repo checkout (`/Users/liam/Documents/code/projects/hivemind-os/scripts/hive-env-add`), so on THIS MAC the repo edit is LIVE the moment it's saved — This Mac's collector already runs push-missing + the new local-only rules (verified: This Mac's `/env` now serves 0 `USEPOD_HOST_*` keys, and its maintenance ran with `lastError: null`). hel1-2/NYC run THEIR OWN checkouts, so they get the fix only after they `git pull`. The per-machine-key hazard was resolved by the follow-up entry below (usepod keys → local-only).
  - Intended commit message: `hive-env sync: periodic --sync-maintenance seeds peers with missing keys (heal strands) + --push-missing dry-run flag`

- 2026-07-06 14:55 PST - Queen voice: free transcription for everyone — caption-source capability matrix (macOS on-device SFSpeechRecognizer + Web Speech) with OpenAI as the paid fallback, zero install bloat
  - Status: Pushed in `45f3216a5`
  - Areas changed: NEW `src/features/queen-voice/caption-source.ts` (capability matrix: native-speech → web-speech → openai-realtime, availability probed once per app session and logged), NEW `src/features/queen-voice/native-speech-caption.ts` (Tauri bridge wrapper), NEW `src/features/queen-voice/web-speech-caption.ts` (reuses the app's established `speechRecognitionConstructor()` from chat-composer), NEW `src/features/queen-voice/recorded-turn.ts` (Whisper-upload turn extracted from the hook for the size cap), `src/features/queen-voice/use-queen-bee-voice.ts`, NEW `src-tauri/speech-native/` (isolated ObjC FFI crate), NEW `src-tauri/src/speech.rs` (`speech_recognition_available`/`start`/`stop` commands + `hivemindos:speech-partial` events), `src-tauri/Cargo.toml` + `Cargo.lock`, `src-tauri/src/lib.rs` (command registration), `src-tauri/Info.plist` (`NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription` — required or `requestAuthorization` terminates the app), `src-tauri/build.rs` + `src-tauri/capabilities/default.json` (the three-way command ACL — caught by `check:tauri-acl`), `scripts/test-queen-clap-activation.mjs`
  - Summary: Live captions and key-free transcription no longer require OpenAI. The caption matrix prefers free sources: (1) macOS `SFSpeechRecognizer` via the Tauri shell — on-device, zero install bloat (the OS ships the model; the objc2 binding crates add kilobytes, not megabytes), fed by a native AVAudioEngine input tap, partials streamed as Tauri events; (2) the browser's Web Speech API in Chrome/Edge browser contexts. The paid OpenAI caption session runs only when neither exists — so when a free source is present it also stops paying the ~$0.017/min whisper caption session. Bigger: the recorder fallback path now runs free captions too and, when caption text exists at commit, uses it AS the transcript — no Whisper upload, no key — making the whole voice loop work keyless on machines with a free source (replies can ride the HivemindOS-models free tier). Structural note flagged for review: every objc2 Speech/AVFAudio binding is an `unsafe fn` and the app crate pins `unsafe_code = "forbid"`, so the FFI lives in a new tiny path crate `src-tauri/speech-native` WITHOUT that lint (the standard Rust unsafe-isolation boundary; the app crate's forbid is untouched). Known trade-offs, named: OS/browser recognizers capture their own mic, so the app's mute button doesn't silence them — caption callbacks and finalize are gated on the mute state instead; caption text wins over Whisper upload at commit even when a key exists (rare: only when realtime STT already failed).
  - Verification: `cargo check --lib` green (both crates, zero warnings, no unsafe in the app crate, re-checked after the build.rs ACL additions); whole-project tsc has zero errors in all touched TS files; eslint clean; `test:queen-clap` 19/19 including new matrix-order and recorder-caption contract assertions (free sources asserted BEFORE openai-realtime); size guard green (hook 1492/1500 after the recorded-turn extraction); `check:tauri-acl` 44 commands in lockstep. NOT runtime-verified: the native mac path needs a real `pnpm tauri:dev` run + mic + one-time speech permission prompt (I cannot exercise the packaged webview mic from here) — the availability probe fails closed, so a broken native path degrades to exactly today's behavior. Web Speech applies to browser sessions; the Tauri WKWebView is expected to lack it (the probe logs `[queen-voice] caption source` to the dev log either way).
  - Intended commit message: `queen voice: caption-source matrix — free on-device (SFSpeechRecognizer) + Web Speech transcription before paid OpenAI; keyless recorder turns`

The collector also refuses to walk hosted-app project roots inside macOS protected app-data locations such as `~/Library/Application Support`, `~/Library/Containers`, and `~/Library/Group Containers`. The follow-up root cause was a collector-launched Hermes worker invoking file search as `rg --files --sortr=modified ... /Users/liam`; collector-spawned Hermes processes now receive safe file-search roots (shared vault, app checkout, Documents, HivemindOS state, Hermes home) and explicit defaults disabling home-wide and macOS app-data searches.

Live mitigation performed on this Mac: collector was temporarily booted out to stop the prompt loop, `~/.hivemindos/syncthing-api-key` was seeded without printing the key and verified `-rw-------`, the collector LaunchAgent was restarted, `/health` was healthy, and a redacted `/syncthing/status` smoke returned HTTP 200 with Syncthing running. Follow-up after the prompt persisted: collector was booted out again, recent TCC logs named `rg` under `com.hivemindos.collector-helper`, process inspection found Hermes-spawned `rg --files --sortr=modified` crawling `/Users/liam`, those exact processes were killed, and the installed Hermes helper on this Mac was patched to reject home-wide/protected app-data file searches before launching `rg` or `find`. After the final restart, process checks found no Hermes worker or broad `rg` crawl beyond the checker itself, and a fresh 5-minute TCC query found zero `display_prompt` or `kTCCServiceSystemPolicyAppData` entries for the collector.

- 2026-07-06 14:05 PST - Queen Bee voice: live captions while speaking (parallel caption stream) — no more "..." until end of utterance
  - Status: Pushed in `45f3216a5`
  - Areas changed: NEW `src/features/queen-voice/stt-caption-stream.ts`, `src/features/queen-voice/use-queen-bee-voice.ts`, `src/features/queen-voice/realtime-stt.ts` (gained `createRealtimeSttPrewarmCache` + `raceSttArmDeadline`, extracted from the hook for the 1500-line cap), `scripts/test-queen-clap-activation.mjs` (new contract assertions)
  - Summary: The server-VAD turn model (`gpt-4o-mini-transcribe`) transcribes a segment only AFTER its auto-commit — protocol probe confirms zero deltas during speech — so the live turn showed "..." for the whole utterance and the words landed 3-4s after the user started talking. The one model that streams words as they're spoken (`gpt-realtime-whisper`, mode "continuous") hard-rejects server VAD, so each armed listening turn now opens a parallel best-effort caption stream on it purely for the live caption; the authoritative turn-session transcript replaces the caption at settle. Guards: authoritative text wins the moment it exists; mute-discard resets captions and a trailing delta can't resurrect a dropped turn; a lost/empty authoritative transcript falls back to the caption the user watched build (visible words never vanish); caption mint failure/stall just leaves the ellipsis — never blocks the turn. Cost note: the caption session (~$0.017/min of listening) runs only while a server-VAD listening turn is armed, alongside the cheaper turn session.

- 2026-07-06 12:07 PST - Dev: unrecoverable ChunkLoadError after hot reloads — proxy no longer kills chunk requests at 2.5s; Turbopack persistent FS cache now opt-in
  - Status: Pushed in `45f3216a5`
  - Areas changed: `next.config.ts`, `scripts/tauri-next-dev.mjs`
  - Summary: Two stacked causes of `ChunkLoadError: Failed to load chunk /_next/static/chunks/... (ecmascript, async loader)` in dev. (1) CONFIRMED on the live 5021 stack: the tauri dev proxy's `proxyTimeoutForRequest` gave non-HTML/non-API requests — i.e. every lazy chunk — only 2.5s before 503ing (`curl` of the exact failing chunk URL returned the proxy's "timed out after 3s" 503 body). A chunk blocked behind a routine Turbopack recompile, or behind the proxy's backend respawn after the Next child dies (observed live: backend crashed and was auto-respawned at 14:10:35 while the proxy stayed up), blows through 2.5s, and Turbopack's async loader turns the 503 into ChunkLoadError; reloads keep failing until the backend settles, which reads as "must restart the dev server". Fix: `/_next/` requests now get 60s so they wait out the compile/boot. (2) `experimental.turbopackFileSystemCacheForDev` flips from default-on to opt-in (`HIVEMINDOS_DEV_FS_CACHE=1`) — it has a known Next 16.2 stale-chunk bug (vercel/next.js discussion #86912) with the same signature. Next 16.2.6 defaults the flag ON (`config-shared.js`), so the explicit `false` is required. Revisit both when stable 16.3 lands (ships default chunk-load retries for Turbopack).
  - Verification: cause (1) diagnosed live — dead upstream on 5121, proxy 503-timeout body on the user-reported chunk URL, backend respawn observed via process start times; the timeout fix itself is `node --check` clean but NOT live-verified (the running proxy predates it — takes effect on the next `pnpm tauri:next-dev` restart). Cause (2): fresh `next dev` boot with the new config shows no experiments banner and writes nothing to the persistent turbopack cache dir through a real page compile; full `tsc --noEmit` passed with the only errors in a torn generated `.next-tauri/verify-5039/dev/types/validator.ts` from the verify boot (deleted; regenerates).
  - Intended commit message: `dev: give /_next/ chunk requests a real proxy timeout; make Turbopack FS cache opt-in (ChunkLoadError)`

  - Status: Pushed
  - Areas changed: `src/features/queen-voice/use-queen-bee-voice.ts` (the energy-VAD loop that decides "you stopped talking" ran ONLY on `requestAnimationFrame`, which WKWebView starves while the page idles — the commit never fired until a click/tap woke rAF; the loop now has the same timer backstop the barge-in watcher uses (~30Hz, active only once rAF has visibly stalled), covering both the realtime-STT and recorder-fallback paths; also exposes the mic `AnalyserNode` as `micAnalyserRef` for the waveform), `src/lib/services/phone/transcription.ts` (comment documenting the live-verified constraint: `gpt-realtime-whisper` 400s on ANY `turn_detection` config at the client_secrets mint, so `turn_detection: null` is load-bearing and end-of-speech must stay client-side), `src/features/queen-voice/VoiceWaveform.tsx` (NEW: live mic-input waveform canvas — 24 mirrored bars envelope-following per-slice RMS of the mic analyser's time-domain signal; rAF + timer backstop so a WKWebView rAF stall can't freeze the meter into a false "mic dead"; slow-timer mode under prefers-reduced-motion; muted = dimmed red flatline; bar color comes from CSS `color` so themes restyle it without JS), `src/features/queen-voice/use-queen-bee-realtime.ts` (mic analyser side-tap off the caption context, exposed the same way so the waveform works in both voice modes), `src/features/queen-voice/QueenBeeVoiceOverlay.tsx` (waveform rendered in the control bar next to the status badge), `src/features/queen-voice/queen-voice.module.css` (waveform colors + hive-light overrides), `.claude/launch.json` + `tsconfig.json` auto-include (verify-5045 isolated-dist-dir throwaway-auth entry, same pattern as verify-5041).
  - Summary: Fixes "I finish speaking and it still looks like it's waiting on me — a click or tap makes it go through": the tap was literally waking `requestAnimationFrame` back up, at which point the frozen VAD loop finally saw the accumulated silence and committed. With the timer backstop the loop keeps ticking through rAF stalls, so turns commit ~600ms after speech ends without any nudge. This also removes the worst of the perceived transcription delay: partial words still stream while speaking (any residual lag there is upstream model latency, `delay: "minimal"` is already set), but the FINAL transcript no longer waits for a tap-triggered commit. NOTE: a server-side fix (OpenAI server VAD in the transcription session) was built first and REVERTED after live verification — `gpt-realtime-whisper` rejects `turn_detection` outright ("Turn detection is not supported for this transcription model"), and shipping it would have silently dropped every session to the Whisper-upload fallback; the constraint is now documented at the mint site. New: an animated waveform in the voice control bar mirroring actual mic input (dim red flatline when muted), so "is she hearing me" is visible at a glance.
  - Verification: Live Playwright (headless Chrome, fake mic, isolated verify server 5045 with throwaway auth): dashboard hydrated, overlay opened via the DOM toggle, control bar + waveform canvas rendered (92x26), canvas pixel-sampled as painted AND animating (alpha sums 14032→14022→77490 across 700ms samples), and the pipeline session reached "Queen Bee is speaking". That run also caught the server-VAD 400 + "[queen-voice] realtime STT unavailable; falling back to Whisper" live — which is what forced the revert; the reverted mint config is byte-identical to the previously shipped, working one. A post-revert re-run rendered the overlay + painted waveform, but the session sat in "Connecting..." under three concurrent dev servers (machine contention), so the post-revert STT mint itself was not re-proven live; further retries were skipped to avoid degrading concurrent sessions. eslint clean on all touched files; whole-project `tsc --noEmit` has zero errors in touched files (only the pre-existing concurrent `company-email-qa.ts:127` error). - 2026-07-05 - Fleet map view: dotted region outlines visible again (both layouts) + de-squished, world-framed projection
  - Status: Pushed
  - Areas changed: `src/components/fleet/map-view.tsx` — FIVE changes. (1) TOKEN SCOPE (the real bug for the default/hive view): `MapView` now imports `fleet-tokens.module.css` and puts `styles.root` on its outer container so it self-provides `--edge-stroke-start`. (2) SINGLE-SOURCE-OF-TRUTH ROBUSTNESS: every SVG use of the edge tokens now goes through module consts `EDGE_STROKE_START`/`EDGE_STROKE_END` that carry inline dark-theme `var(..., fallback)` — so the map can never render invisible again even if mounted with zero external token scope (`.root` still supplies theme-aware values on top). (3) STYLING: the coastline `<g>` `strokeWidth` 0.7 → 1.4, `strokeDasharray` `"0.8 3"` → `"0.1 4.5"` + `strokeLinecap="round"` (near-zero dashes → evenly spaced round dots), dropped the extra `opacity={0.55}`. (4) DE-SQUISH: `createFleetProjection` now clamps axis anisotropy to `MAP_MAX_ANISOTROPY = 1.8` (widening — never cropping — the too-zoomed axis around the same center), so a globe-spanning / low-latitude-spread fleet no longer stretches continents ~5x vertically. `MAP_MAX_ANISOTROPY` is the single squish knob. (5) WORLD-FRAMED VERTICAL CENTER: `mapContentBounds` now folds the projected coastline latitude extent (`COASTLINE_LAT_MIN/MAX`, the data bbox) into the VERTICAL bounds only, so the initial recenter (and the drag clamp, which otherwise re-centers on pins) frames the map on the visible landmass — killing the dead band above the map that a northern-only fleet produced. Horizontal center still follows the fleet pins.
  - Summary: Answers "the fleet map used to have dotted outlines of the regions — where did they go?" Two compounding causes. FIRST (styling): commit `c481b58d` swapped two bold hand-drawn continent silhouettes for real Natural Earth 1:110m coastlines but kept the old faint styling (0.7px hairline, ~0.27 effective alpha, mostly-gap dash) — two big blobs survived that, but ~70–119 fragmented real coastlines dissolved into near-invisible stipple. SECOND, and the reason the DEFAULT (hive) fleet view showed NOTHING even in classic-visible cases: the coastline stroke is `var(--edge-stroke-start)`, a token defined only on `.root` in `fleet-tokens.module.css`. The classic `FleetView` wraps its map in `.root` (so the token resolves), but `FleetHiveView` never imports those tokens — so under the hive layout the var was undefined, SVG `stroke` fell back to its initial `none`, and the coastline paths rendered fully invisible regardless of width/dash. Making `MapView` carry its own `.root` (the same pattern `HexTile` already uses) makes it self-sufficient and theme-aware under any layout.
  - Verification: The outline fix (1–3) is CONFIRMED LIVE — the user hard-reloaded hive→map and the dotted continents render (two screenshots). The de-squish (4) is CONFIRMED LIVE too — the user's screenshot shows proportioned continents, and flagged the resulting empty band above, which (5) addresses. Supporting proofs: (a) CSS cascade reproduced in a real WebKit engine (`qlmanage` on HTML) — the identical 119-path coastline `<g>` renders BLANK with no `.root` ancestor and visible once the token is provided. (b) De-squish rendered from the real fleet (Helsinki/NY/Hong Kong) at three anisotropy caps; the user chose 1.8x, which the committed projection reproduces exactly. (c) The recenter fix was rendered via the FULL pipeline (projection + anisotropy + pin/edge bounds + pan) both ways: pin-centered reproduces the user's dead-band-on-top screenshot, content-centered frames the whole world with a small balanced margin — the exact math now in `mapContentBounds`. `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0 after every change. Also verified in source that the drag clamp (`clampAxis`) would otherwise override a content-centered pan back to pin-centered when the pin bbox is smaller than the viewport — which is why the fix lives in `mapContentBounds` (feeding both recenter and clamp), not just the recenter effect. NOT yet verified by me: the live in-app render of change (5) specifically (needs one more reload to eyeball; it re-anchors the map vertically in both hive and classic).
  - Intended commit message: `fleet-map: fix invisible outlines in hive layout + de-squish and world-frame the projection`

- 2026-07-04 18:03 +07 - Fleet animation breathes to the Queen's voice while she speaks in voice chat
  - Status: Pushed
  - Areas changed: `src/lib/audio/queen-voice-amplitude.ts` (NEW — a shared, framework-agnostic "how loud is the Queen right now" channel: an imperative 0..1 `level` + `speaking` singleton read at 60fps without React state, a WeakMap output-analyser tap, an envelope-following RMS pump hook `useQueenVoiceLevelPump`, and a DOM-var pulse hook `useQueenVoicePulse`), `src/lib/audio/realtime-pcm-stream-player.ts` (side-tap the streamed-TTS worklet `gain` into the shared analyser), `src/features/queen-voice/spoken-reply-playback.ts` (side-tap the buffered-clip `source` too), `src/features/queen-voice/use-queen-bee-voice.ts` (pipeline hook: create the shared output analyser at session start, drive the pump while `phase === "speaking"`), `src/features/queen-voice/use-queen-bee-realtime.ts` (realtime hook: build an analysis-only AudioContext off her remote WebRTC track and drive the same pump), `src/components/fleet/orbital-graph.tsx` (graph particle-sphere: core glow + particle cloud swell/brighten with her live amplitude each frame), `src/components/fleet-hive/HiveStage.tsx` + `src/components/fleet-hive/fleet-hive.css` (default hive Queen cell: the honey halo tracks `--queen-amp` while she speaks, with a subtler sympathetic pulse on the Queen herself; idle breathe unchanged when silent; reduced-motion tames it to opacity-only).
  - Summary: While the Queen is speaking during voice chat, the big fleet animation now breathes and pulses in time with her actual voice — the exact beat, volume, and cadence — instead of a fixed idle loop. Both fleet visualizations react: the graph-mode particle sphere and the default hive-mode Queen cell. The moment she stops, both settle back to their normal resting animation. There was no voice-level signal in the app before this (the only meters measured your mic, for barge-in) — this reads her real OUTPUT audio via Web Audio analysers on every playback path (streamed local TTS, buffered/cloud TTS clips, and the OpenAI Realtime stream) and envelope-follows it (fast attack, slower release) so onsets punch on the beat and syllables read as a smooth breathe.
  - Design notes: the amplitude is pushed through an imperative singleton + one edge-only "speaking" CustomEvent, deliberately NOT React context/state — a 60fps `setState` would re-render the whole fleet tree (`AgentsPanel` is memoized precisely to dodge the voice waveform). The graph reads the singleton inside its existing rAF; the hive cell is driven by writing `--queen-amp` on the DOM node imperatively, so HiveStage's fleet-poll re-renders never touch the 60fps path. The pump/pulse loops only run while she's speaking and carry a 30Hz `setInterval` backstop for WKWebView's idle-page rAF starvation (same guard as the barge-in watcher and the Lottie player). The pipeline analyser is a pure side-tap (its upstream is already routed to the destination); the realtime path builds a dedicated context `stream → source → analyser → zero-gain → destination` so the analyser is "pulled" on WebKit while staying silent (the `<audio>` element is still what you hear).
  - Verification: focused `pnpm exec eslint` on all seven touched TS/TSX files exited 0 (`--max-warnings=0`); full `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit --pretty false --skipLibCheck` reports zero errors for any changed file (one TS 5.7 typed-array generic error — `getByteTimeDomainData` wants `Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>` — was caught and fixed); all touched files are well under the 1500-line cap (largest is `use-queen-bee-voice.ts` at 1376). NOT verified by me (needs a real voice session on the desktop app — no mic/TTS/Realtime backend is exercisable headlessly here): the actual audio→animation sync on both paths, and specifically that the realtime analysis-only AudioContext resumes under WKWebView rather than staying suspended (if it doesn't, the realtime pulse is simply idle and playback is unaffected — this is the one claim I'd most expect to need on-device confirmation; the pipeline TTS path shares the already-unlocked session context and is the safer bet). To see it: open Queen voice chat, and while she talks, watch the fleet graph (graph mode) or the central Queen hex (default hive mode).
  - Intended commit message: `fleet: pulse the fleet animation to the Queen's live voice amplitude during voice chat`

- 2026-07-04 - Queen voice: barge-in now works even when you start talking exactly as a new sentence begins
  - Status: Pushed
  - Areas changed: `src/features/queen-voice/barge-in-detector.ts` (new `peakFloor` state = the loudest echo floor observed this reply, i.e. the ceiling of her residual bleed; a gated peak-keyed guard so a NON-initial resume-recalibration window absorbs only frames at or below `max(minRms, peakFloor * guardMultiplier)` — a louder frame is provably the user and falls through to the normal trigger path so it can break in mid-window; the guard is GATED on `bleedEstablished` (peakFloor risen at least `establishedFloorRatio`× above `initialFloor`) and latched per window at `requestBargeInRecalibration` time, so a silent grace or a first chunk after a slow synth falls back to today's unconditional absorb; two new tuning knobs `guardMultiplier` 1.8 and `establishedFloorRatio` 1.6), `scripts/test-queen-voice-working.mjs` (two new gate guards; the existing self-interrupt and resume-recalibration guards are untouched), `scratchpad/barge-in-wiring-sim.mjs` (rebuilt end-to-end wiring sim driving the REAL detector).
  - Summary: Fixes the residual "onset latch" flagged in the prior entry. If you started talking within the ~600ms exactly as a new sentence chunk resumed, the resume-recalibration window absorbed your voice into the echo floor at 0.2/frame, pushing the trigger threshold to ~2.75× your own volume, which `floorBlendBelow` then self-sustained — so you stayed deaf for a couple of natural pauses (~3.5s worst case in simulation). The detector now tracks `peakFloor`; once her bleed is established, a resume window lets any frame louder than that ceiling through to the trigger path instead of absorbing it, so a barge-in coinciding with a sentence onset breaks in mid-window. The fix is entirely inside the detector — the per-chunk resume windows were already opened by the existing wiring (`use-queen-bee-voice.ts` + `spoken-reply-playback.ts`), so no playback/hook code changed. Simulation against the real detector: onset-coincidence interrupts now fire ≤460ms (was ~3.5s / never), mid-chunk still ~440ms, and zero false self-triggers across normal bleed (0.03), loud bleed (0.06), and a first chunk after a slow synth.
  - The trap avoided: an UNGATED peak-keyed guard breaks the pinned 2026-07-02 self-interrupt test — its grace-is-silence scenario never establishes a bleed reference, so the guard would let her own first resumed bleed pass the amplitude discriminator and self-trigger. This is also a REAL first-chunk case when synth TTFB exceeds the 600ms grace. The `bleedEstablished` gate closes it by falling back to unconditional absorb until her bleed is actually observed; the pinned self-interrupt guard stays green, unmodified.
  - Pre-existing flaw named (NOT introduced here, out of scope): the nominal trigger is `echoFloor × 2.75`, but `floorBlendAbove` drifts the floor up 0.004/frame during the 420ms sustain, so the EFFECTIVE barge-in floor is ~3.7× the echo level, not 2.75× — measured on the plain (no-window) path where the new guard is inert: over a 0.06 floor a user at 3.0–3.3× never breaks in, 3.7×+ fires at ~432ms. A realistic conversational barge-in (~0.25–0.4 RMS over 0.03–0.06 residual echo = 5–13×) is unaffected and the sim models that; flagged as a follow-up.
  - Verification: `node scripts/test-queen-voice-working.mjs` all green including the two new onset-coincidence guards AND the unchanged self-interrupt / resume-recalibration guards; `pnpm test` 88/90 vs 88/90 baseline (same two pre-existing reds — `check-sizes` on `agent-telemetry-collector.mjs`/`kanban-board.module.css` and `hive-action-route-drift` on `company-revenue/route.ts`, none touched here); focused eslint + full `tsc --noEmit --skipLibCheck` exit 0; `node scratchpad/barge-in-wiring-sim.mjs` ALL CHECKS PASS (onset ≤460ms, mid-chunk ~440ms, 0 self-triggers, before/after contrast shows the pre-fix window never breaks through). NOT verified by me: the actual on-device barge-in with a real mic and real speaker echo — the watcher is client-side and a node sim cannot exercise WKWebView AEC, so this needs one real voice session on the desktop app.
  - Intended commit message: `queen voice: fix onset-coincidence barge-in latch (gated peak-keyed echo guard)`

- 2026-07-04 - Queen voice: you can interrupt her mid-sentence again, and the "connected" chime only plays once
  - Status: Pushed
  - Areas changed: `src/features/queen-voice/barge-in-detector.ts` (echo-floor recalibration window `recalibrateMs` 1000→600, with a comment on why it must stay short), `src/features/queen-voice/use-queen-bee-voice.ts` (removed the per-chunk-seam `activity.underrunAt` stamp that opened a suppression window at every sentence boundary; the watcher's rAF loop now has a `setInterval` backstop that runs the tick when rAF has stalled — a WKWebView starvation guard mirroring `src/components/ui/lottie-player.tsx`), `src/features/queen-voice/spoken-reply-playback.ts` (recalibration is now anchored at the actual audio RESUME — `onFirstByte` for the streaming path, before `source.start()` for the buffered path — instead of the chunk seam), `src/features/queen-voice/QueenBeeVoiceOverlay.tsx` (deleted `playQueenThinkingSound` and the phase-transition effect that replayed the activation `scifi-ping.wav` on every "thinking" turn), `scripts/test-queen-voice-working.mjs` (new regression guard: a user talking after a resume-recalibration window still breaks in within the sustain window; existing self-interrupt guards stay green).
  - Summary: Two fixes. (1) BARGE-IN — the barge-in watcher stamped every sentence-chunk boundary as a playback "underrun," which opened a 1000ms echo-floor recalibration window at each seam; inside a window the detector cannot trigger and blends the mic (your voice included) into the floor, so within ~170ms the threshold became 2.75× your own volume and stayed there for the rest of her reply (confirmed by simulation against the real detector: 0/100 interrupt attempts succeeded). Real underruns are already reported separately by the player's `onUnderrun`, and the resumed bleed that recalibration actually guards against returns at the next chunk's audio onset — so the fix anchors recalibration at the audio RESUME (not the seam) and shortens the window to cover just the bleed onset. Result (same simulation): mid-sentence interrupts now fire ~420ms, zero false self-interrupts. (2) CHIME — the connect "bing" was being reused as a per-turn "thinking" cue, so it replayed on every tool-call turn; that cue is removed, leaving only the once-per-session activation sound.
  - Known limitation (NOW FIXED by the newer 2026-07-04 entry above — "barge-in now works even when you start talking exactly as a new sentence begins"): if you begin talking within the ~600ms exactly as a NEW sentence starts, a residual floor-poisoning latch could take a couple of natural pauses (~3.5s in simulation, worst case) to break through, because the resume window still absorbed your voice if it opened mid-word. Removing that latch needed a peak-keyed detector change that collides with the pinned 2026-07-02 self-interrupt regression test; the follow-up landed it behind a `bleedEstablished` gate so the pinned test stays green. Still pending: the on-device ear-test with a real mic.
  - Verification: eslint + filtered `tsc` clean on all four touched source files; `pnpm test` 88/90 (the 2 reds are concurrent sessions' `check-sizes` on `agent-telemetry-collector.mjs`/`kanban-board.module.css` and a `hive-action-route-drift` on `company-revenue/route.ts` — none are touched here); `node scripts/test-queen-voice-working.mjs` all green including the new guard and the unchanged self-interrupt guards; end-to-end wiring proven by a node simulation driving the REAL detector (old seam-anchor vs new resume-anchor); voice pipeline still audible (`POST speak` → 200 audio/wav 165KB). NOT verified by me: the actual on-device barge-in and the single chime — both need a real mic and the desktop app (the watcher is client-side; a curl can't exercise it).
  - Intended commit message: `queen voice: restore mid-sentence barge-in (anchor echo recalibration at audio resume) + stop replaying the connect chime`

- 2026-07-04 - ROOT-CAUSE FIX for Tauri dev-app lag: dashboard-state invokes no longer grind a 33MB store on the UI-process main thread
  - Status: Pushed
  - Areas changed: `src/features/dashboard/dashboard-storage.ts` (new `compactFleetSnapshotsForPersist`: persisted fleet snapshots capped to the 128 most recently checked — the merge never evicts, so ephemeral per-PID hermes agents had accumulated 2,822 entries / 30.6MB under `hivemindos.fleetSnapshots.v1`), `src/features/dashboard/DashboardApp.tsx` (persist effect uses the helper; net −6 lines), `src-tauri/src/dashboard_state.rs` (`dashboard_state_read`/`dashboard_state_write` are now async so they run on the async runtime instead of the main thread; the write response no longer echoes the full store — the only caller reads just `ok`), `src-tauri/Cargo.toml` (`[profile.dev.package."*"] opt-level = 2`: dev builds optimize dependencies so debug-mode serde_json/tauri/wry can't stall the UI thread; app crate stays unoptimized for fast iteration).
  - Summary: The dev-app lag was NOT machine contention, transparency, or paint effects. `sample` of the live debug app caught the smoking gun: every dashboard interaction persists a remembered value via `dashboard_state_write`, and wry delivers sync-command invokes on the UI-process main thread — which read+parsed the 33.5MB `~/.hivemindos/dashboard-state.json`, cloned it twice, re-serialized it to disk, then serialized the ENTIRE store again as the (unused) IPC response, all in an opt-level-0 debug binary (904/7476 main-thread samples in serde_json during a light 10s probe). WKWebView input events and layer-tree commits queue behind that same main thread → the 130–200ms frames and 4–8s stalls in the Safari Timeline. The 33MB store itself was a data leak: fleet snapshots persisted one entry per ephemeral hermes PID, never pruned. Chrome was fast because browser builds use the HTTP route in another process; packaged builds were fast because release opt-level 3 hides the cost.
  - Verification: `sample` of the original pre-fix debug app (pid 60604) during a light 10s probe caught 904/7476 main-thread samples inside `serde_json` serializing the store — the smoking gun. After rebuild+relaunch (the `opt-level=2` dep rebuild lands a fresh binary at 16:56, watcher auto-relaunches), a matched 10s activation-burst `sample` of the live app (pid 94745) that actually fired a persist (13 `dashboard_state` frames present) shows those frames on `tokio-rt-worker` threads and **0 `serde_json`/`dashboard_state` frames on the main thread** (main thread parked in kernel waits) — the async commands confirmed off-thread end-to-end (also visible in the binary's symbol table: `dashboard_state_read/write` now emit future-closure symbols). The store self-healed on the first persist through the new path: 33.5MB → 1.7MB (`fleetSnapshots` 30.6MB → 739KB, exactly 128 agents). `pnpm exec eslint src/features/dashboard/dashboard-storage.ts` clean; `pnpm test` gate 89/90 — same red as the session baseline (`check-sizes`, now only the two other-session files `agent-telemetry-collector.mjs` + `kanban-board.module.css`; DashboardApp.tsx dropped back under its allowance). NOT mine: `pnpm exec eslint` on `DashboardApp.tsx` reports one error at :4590 (`revealKanbanTaskRef.current` assigned during render) — absent from committed HEAD, so it belongs to a concurrent session's uncommitted edit in the shared tree; left untouched. Remaining user check: real clicks/view-switches feel instant in the dev app window.
  - Intended commit message: `perf: dashboard-state invokes off the main thread + prune persisted fleet snapshots (dev-app lag root cause)`

- 2026-07-04 03:30 +08 - ROOT-CAUSE FIX for Tauri click-lag: make the window opaque (transparent:true forced a non-opaque WKWebView → whole-scene alpha-blend every frame)
  - Status: Pushed (needs a Rust rebuild to take effect + on-device re-profile to confirm)
  - Areas changed: `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` (main window: `transparent: true` → `false`, and REMOVED `backgroundColor: "#080a0f"`), `scripts/tauri-dev-signed.mjs` (reverted the earlier dev-only `--config transparent:false` overlay — it was a no-op because it kept `backgroundColor`, and the real fix is now in the committed config).
  - Root cause (source-confirmed, 5 independent research agents + wry source read): a real Safari Web Inspector Timeline of the actual Tauri WKWebView showed the per-click lag is NOT JS (script 8%, layout 6%) and NOT CSS paint (backdrop-filter/box-shadow/filter/animation all force-disabled on-device → still laggy; `document.documentElement.className` confirmed the disable was live). The cost is "unaccounted" WebKit PAINT+COMPOSITE — ~28 frames in 22s, interaction frames ~130-200ms (≈5-7fps) vs the SAME app <16ms in Chrome/Blink. Mechanism: `wry-0.55.1/src/wkwebview/mod.rs:368` sets the private `drawsBackground=NO` KVC key when `transparent || background_color.is_some()`, and `:454` calls `setOpaque(false)` when a background_color is set → the WKWebView root CALayer is NON-OPAQUE. Safari has no dedicated compositor thread (reuses macOS Core Animation), so a non-opaque root forces WindowServer to alpha-blend the ENTIRE window against the desktop backdrop every composite pass — memory-bandwidth-heavy, exactly the profiled unaccounted time. Blink avoids it (opaque window + dedicated compositor). The transparency was visually UNUSED — the app paints solid `#080a0f` everywhere (layout.tsx:35, globals.css) — so opaque is a visual no-op. My earlier `--config transparent:false` failed because it kept `backgroundColor`, which independently triggers the non-opaque path (per the wry guard).
  - Verification: config validated (wry guard `transparent || background_color.is_some()` now evaluates FALSE → opaque); `node --check` on the reverted launcher; `pnpm test` gate 88/90 (same pre-existing baseline). NOT yet confirmed: the on-device speedup — this is a NATIVE window change so it needs `pnpm tauri:dev` to REBUILD the Rust shell, then re-run the same Web Inspector Timeline. Expected: interaction frames drop from 130-200ms toward <16ms. Falsifiable: if frames barely move, transparency wasn't the dominant cost and the next levers are content-visibility:auto on the all-mounted kanban cards + reducing the 44 overflow:scroll layers (research captured these). Known minor caveat: removing `backgroundColor` may cause a brief default-background flash before CSS paints on cold load — the dev loading shell covers most of it; if annoying, set an opaque NSWindow background in Rust setup (doesn't re-trigger non-opaque).
  - Intended commit message: `desktop perf: opaque window (transparent:false + drop backgroundColor) to fix WKWebView per-frame full-scene alpha-blend — the real click-lag root cause`
